📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shopping for wallpaper is an excellent way to discover just how indecisive you can be. Between painterly florals, graphic stripes, and whimsical prints, narrowing down the options is practically a full-time job. And that's before you get into the textures, finishes, and the peel-and-stick versus traditional wallpaper debate. There's a pattern for just about every room, taste, and level of commitment. Luckily, we've done some of the research for you.

Wallpaper can also do a lot more than cover four walls. A scenic mural can feel more like large-scale art, and built-in bookshelves can get a refresh simply by lining their backs. Even a drawer lined with your favorite print can be a delightful little surprise, not to mention a low-stakes project for a first-time DIYer. Whether you're ready to commit to an entire room or just want to test the waters, these are the wallpaper brands worth adding to your Pinterest board.

In a recent development, consider these pinstripes a subtle way to showcase your team loyalty. This print suits any number of installation methods, whether you prefer peel-and-stick, pre-pasted rolls, vinyl, or grasscloth. There are even metallic accents you can choose for added glamour.

Sources indicate that A geometric print awakens a space in a jiffy, and these Bauhaus circles are prime for a midcentury modern abode. Picture it surrounding a fireplace mantle or in an entryway. Adding the print to a ceiling is an unexpected move that gives the space a wow factor.

Wayfair doesn’t miss a thing—hidden amongst their enormous catalog of affordable furniture and decor is a considerable collection of wallpaper. Every print and pattern under the sun is represented here, from chevron to toile to florals.

Sources indicate that this tile-inspired temporary wallpaper can work as a backsplash for a “blah” kitchen, on the walls surrounding your soaking tub, or as panels on cabinets. The tiles have a crisp look and, honestly, look pretty close to the real deal.

Recent findings suggest that when in doubt, toile it out. Toile patterns are an easy way to introduce elevated detail. Their classic, subtle details keep things simple, but dynamic. Plus, they work in many different spaces—a bedroom (child or adult), a bathroom, a backsplash, or a living room decorated with early Baroque pieces.

Serena & Lily offers a small, curated collection of nautical, floral, and patterned designs (many that include natural elements like hydrangeas, palm leaves, and sea shells) for dressing up a nursery or bedroom. The color palettes tend to be soft blues, beiges, and variegated greens that play up to the coastal aesthetic.

In a recent development, for Wedgwood fans, this antique-style print is a serene surprise. (Just keep in mind that it’s not removable before taking on a full project.) Pro tip: The brand recommends using a wallpaper liner if you’re working with uneven wall surfaces to keep the finished project smooth.

Here’s another understated option with subtle texture, available in pastels like pistachio, sand, and sky. The muted tones make a great backdrop to any design style, lending the whole room a sense of calm.

Recent findings suggest that while browsing for furniture, we stumbled upon Anthropologie’s robust collection of elevated wallpaper designs that span sophisticated florals and chinoiserie, damasks, and truly special geometric patterns. Their knack for hand-block prints, Renaissance revival, and arabesque designs makes them a no-brainer for any room that you want to be an absolute showstopper. Don’t sleep on their wall murals, too.).

Green bedrooms are trending, but if you want to up the ante on the soothing factor, look no further than this dreamy chinoiserie mural with cerulean-feathered songbirds and lemons to give your space a bit of joie de vivre.

In a recent development, showcasing Southern artist Jordan Connelly's signature painterly style, these repeating seashells are a non-cliché way to bring a coastal feel to your space. Plus, the tonal color palette makes this great for a child's bedroom or bathroom.

For subtle stripes and vintage-inspired botanicals, McGee & Co.’s small-but-mighty wallpaper selection is there to fulfill your elevated farmhouse needs. Designed to perfectly suit her existing selection of furniture and decor, McGee’s wallpaper serves as a statement finishing touch, one you soon wouldn’t be able to envision your hallway or powder room without. You’ll even find her take on antique Morris and Co. florals through her pastel-hued collaboration.

This moody floral is ideal for crafting a cozy corner in a bedroom or den, especially in the navy colorway. Pair with the matching throw pillows for a pattern-drenching moment.

Sometimes all it takes is a simple stripe to elevate your space. Thanks to its neutral colorway, you can liven it up or tone it down to your heart's content with a blend of upholstery tones, artwork, and decor. Treat it like paint, just with a bit more oomph.

Chasing Paper is our go-to when we want something elevated that has a dash of whimsy. The brand is known for designer collaborations, too. Most recently, Fariha Nasir translated the South Asian art of block printing into wallpaper with floral garlands and tapestry-like designs. All Chasing Paper patterns come in four options: faux grasscloth, performance vinyl, peel-and-stick, and traditional paper. While we checked out samples in all materials, we can vouch for the durability and crisp pattern of peel-and-stick. They also offer tile decals (that happen to work as contact paper to upgrade worn countertops.).

Recent findings suggest that as far as peel-and-stick wallpapers go, the self-adhesive poly-woven fabric of Chasing Paper is second to none. “I am no stranger to putting up peel-and-stick and the Peonies pattern I used for my home office is on par with luxe wallcoverings for heritage brands,” states contributor Yelena Alpert. “The paper adhered securely to the wood paneling, but it had no trouble coming up if I had to realign a panel. The best part is that I did not get any air bubbles—it’s a DIY miracle.” While Alpert opted for the bold red-and-grey colorway that reminded her of Diana Vreeland’s crimson interiors, a toned-down gold-and-cream is also available.

In a recent development, for fans of cabana stripes, this design from Chasing Paper agrees with minimalists and maximalists alike. It’s tough to choose between seven colorways (though we are partial to daisy yellow), which are all great for different purposes: mud rooms, nurseries, beachy bathrooms, or a design-forward living room.

The contemporary meets midcentury aesthetic of West Elm seamlessly carries through to their wallpaper collection, which includes fetching grasscloth designs and designer collaborations, like their latest with design studio Pierce & Ward. Patterns are geometric and playful but not kitschy, and work perfectly for accent walls. You can also find a few animal print designs and artsy figure drawings that are suitable for powder rooms.

It has been revealed that add this organic, playful peel-and-stick wallpaper to your wish list. Those who aren’t homeowners will love how easy the cleanup is for removable wallpaper when moving day rolls around. And when it comes to wallpaper motifs, simple is sometimes better—the soothing neutrals and distinct geometric pattern will elevate and simultaneously calm any room or nook.

Let’s say you want something neutral and textured but grasscloth is not your cup of tea. The Piece & Ward Floral Lattice design is a worthy alternative as it gives the wall a 3D moment but won’t compete with furnishings, especially if you’re into warm wooden pieces. Include ceramic pieces in your home decor to give the entire space a layered look.

Sources indicate that the celebrated 19th century British designer, William Morris, was a traditionalist devoted to his craft in the midst of the Industrial Revolution. He taught himself block printing techniques to create more than 20 nature-inspired patterns that encapsulate the Arts & Crafts Movement. His design brand Morris & Co. was established in 1861 and has shown no signs of slowing down as contemporary designers continue to incorporate the wallpaper patterns in their projects. Each wallpaper design is batch-printed in the United Kingdom, making it a good practice to order all rolls at the same time to ensure the dye lots are the same.

The Strawberry Thief is one of Morris & Co.’s most popular patterns and was inspired by the birds that would pop into Kelmscott Manor, Morris’s home in Oxfordshire, to steal the berries from the kitchen. “The gravure printed paper has this heirloom quality that makes it feel as if it is directly plucked from the archives,” says contributor Yelena Alpert, who has samples in indigo and crimson colorways. “Each cheeky bird is about the size of my hand, and the foliage has this watercolor quality. It would look amazing above wood paneling, painted or not.”.

Part of the Morris & Co., pattern appeal is that each floral motif is actually on a grid, giving it a certain rhythm. Pimpernel, another favorite, is ornate in the way that the swirls repeat without overwhelming the eye. This design is seen in the Kelmscott House dining room and was chosen by Morris himself. It comes in 16 colorways that span blues, greens, and venture into burgundy.

According to recent reports, more than just a place to find scalloped accent chairs and fashion-inspired collaborations (Aimee Song and Carly Cushnie, anyone?), Lulu & Georgia also offers wallpaper. Of course, you can find the likes of Morris & Co. and Scalamandre, but the brand also has their own in-house line. Design stars Sarah Sherman Samuel and Jake Arnold have also lent their talents to this stock with luxe grasscloths and ornate botanicals. Here you’ll find perfect pairings for your velvet bed frame or curved sofa.

Designed by Sarah Sherman Samuel, this intricate print is made more luxe with the addition of a subtle paper weave, adding texture to the linework style drawings.

Polka dots are a playful addition to standard pinstripes, creating a whimsical gateway for those more inclined to traditional styles of design.

Industry observers note that beloved for their quirky paint color names like Disco Nap (a pale acid yellow) and Silver Lake Dad (a stormy blue grey), Backdrop Home also makes patterned wallcoverings that perfectly color-match their hues. Once absorbed into Schumacher’s family of brands, Backdrop also introduced archival prints, textured sisal, and peel-and-stick wallpaper options. Backdrop Home offers the kind of whimsical designs that you can’t find elsewhere. Swirling snakes and quilt-like geometric prints that instantly liven up any room, and will have you saying, ‘Oh yeah, that’s Backdrop.’.

Sources indicate that taken from the archives of fabric brand Schumacher, Backdrop Home’s iteration takes notes from John Groth’s original 1957 fabric. The sketched horses and riders pair perfectly with the aptly named Ghost Ranch, a warm terracotta-esque brown.

Available in both sisal and plainweave, this geometric print becomes more subtle the more square footage you stretch it across. While wholly impactful in tight spaces like a closet or powder room, this print transforms in large scale, becoming almost hypnotic with its various plum tones.

In a recent development, with a stock full of ornate prints and patterns inspired by historic European textiles, Transylvanian brand Mind the Gap has something for every design style. Heritage-style plaids for the sophisticated sit alongside Eastern-influenced Ikats and jungle motifs for the maximalist. There are also plenty of coordinating textiles if you prefer to pattern-drench your space.

Inspired by upholstery textiles, this maximalist stripe gives the look of fabric-covered walls without the need for a specialty installation.

Vibrant and eclectic, this floral tapestry-style wallcovering recalls early Germanic florals and the brand founders’ childhoods in Transylvania.

In a recent development, york knows wallpaper. The wallcoverings producer has been around for more than 100 years and still dips into the archive to bring back designs from the early 18th century. The Susquehanna Valley, Pennsylvania, factory is the oldest and largest wallcovering producer in the United States. Even if you’re not into heirloom patterns, their designer series includes collections from Magnolia Home, Rifle Paper Co., Missoni, and LoveShackFancy, among many others.

In a recent development, the Italian knitwear firm Missoni is now accessible to the more budget-conscious clientele with its upcoming premium peel-and-stick collection (which also includes the iconic zigzags and florals). The Fireworks pattern is almost like a non-dizzying version of the 1990s Magic Eye motif. “I just ordered all three colorways—natural, mauve, and warm grey—to help me decide which one would look best as an accent wall behind my bed,” Alpert says. “Even though it is peel-and-stick, the texture is that of real wallpaper—smooth and velvety!”.

A tonal geometric print adds just enough visual interest without overwhelming the eye. This print was designed by Joanna Gaines and the Magnolia Home team to combine the beauty of an artist's sketch with the structure of a true geometric pattern.

Boutique wallpaper brand Hygge & West are beloved for their colorful takes on botanicals and geometric patterns. With best sellers like the Alpine Garden and Bloom, the brand seems to have expertly mastered the ability to create visually striking designs that never overwhelm your space, no matter how small. Even in a powder room, the motifs draw the eye in just the right way, complementing your space instead of taking it over. However, if you’re a maximalist, there are definitely patterns for you too.

The Arcade print blends Pac-Man-like shapes and transforms them into a repeat that’s not dissimilar from a quilt block.

One of the brand’s best-sellers, Alpine Garden’s colors pop against the black background that adds a bit of moodiness to typically saccharine florals.

Recent findings suggest that not every home comes with a century's worth of character, but that doesn't mean it can't look the part. Best known for its period-inspired lighting and hardware, Rejuvenation brings that same appreciation for Old-World charm to its wallpaper collection. Think intricate botanicals, heritage-inspired prints, and textural takes on grasscloth and sisal that make even a upcoming build feel storied.

Recent findings suggest that sisal doesn't have to stay underfoot. This Hoffmann print recreates the natural, woven texture in a peel-and-stick wallpaper, bringing instant warmth and dimension to the room.

The soft blue-and-cream palette keeps the Fencott print's small-scale leaf motif from feeling too busy.

Are you more drawn to the cozy, muted tones of winter or the vibrant colors of summer? At Claret & Key, you can have your favorite season on your walls year-round. The brand offers its wallpaper patterns in four seasonal color palettes, each giving the same design a different personality. And if none feels quite right, you can dip into the brand's extensive color library to create a combination of your own. Designs are also available in traditional, heavy-grade, and removable options.

In a recent development, romeo's hand-drawn leaves give you the look of a custom mural without having to hire an actual muralist. The trailing foliage gives the walls a sense of movement, making this an especially fitting choice for a reading nook straight out of an English country house.

Nellie, on the other hand, brings a little sunshine to the nursery or kid’s room with its vintage-inspired lemon print. The Spring palette reads more neutral, with subdued tones that keep the citrus motif from feeling too playful.

Hang that framed landscape elsewhere—your walls deserve a full view. Crate & Barrel's scenic wallpaper murals turn blank walls into sprawling gardens and leafy landscapes that look as though an artist painted them right onto the surface. Its exclusive wallpaper collection is designed in-house and made in the USA by York Wallcoverings, with plenty of stripes, florals, and textured designs for those who prefer something more understated. If you're having trouble deciding, up to 10 free wallpaper samples should help narrow the field.

Industry observers note that there's a reason Jardin has all the charm of a hand-painted landscape—it originally started as one. Painted in watercolor on canvas paper, the tree-lined scene was digitally scanned to preserve every brushstroke and subtle shift in color. The result is a dreamy, softly layered landscape that gives your walls the look of an original watercolor.

Recent findings suggest that vivaldi puts a wallpaper spin on the classic verdure tapestry. Printed on natural sisal, it even has the texture to play the part.

Industry observers note that perpetual futures are the engine room of crypto trading. Centralized exchanges processed $85.3 trillion in perps trading volume in 2025 alone, according to CoinGecko's State of Crypto Perpetuals Report 2026, and the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) describes perps as the dominant form of crypto derivatives trading.

Recent findings suggest that they aren't only for crypto, either. Exchanges now offer perps on stocks, commodities and currencies, and Decrypt has become the first news publisher to offer perps trading, powered by Solana exchange Phoenix.

This guide explains what futures are, what makes perpetual futures different, how funding rates and liquidations work, and what to know before trading them.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

To understand perpetual futures, it helps to start with ordinary futures.

A futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a set date in the future. Futures have been used for centuries: farmers used them to lock in prices for crops before harvest, and today they are traded on everything from oil and wheat to stock indexes and Bitcoin, on regulated exchanges such as CME.

Traders use futures for two main reasons. Hedgers use them to protect against price swings; an airline might buy oil futures to lock in fuel costs, for example. Speculators use them to bet on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

In a recent development, traditional futures have an expiry date. When a contract expires, it settles, either by delivering the asset or, more often, by paying out the difference in cash. Traders who want to keep their position open must "roll" it into a new contract, which can add costs and complexity.

Perpetual futures, often shortened to "perps" or "perpetual swaps," work like futures, but with one key difference: they never expire. Traders can hold a position for as long as they like, provided they have enough collateral to keep it open.

The idea was proposed by Yale economist Robert Shiller in a 1993 paper as a way to create markets for assets that are hard to trade directly. Perps took off in crypto. Crypto exchange BitMEX, widely credited with bringing perps to crypto, launched a perpetual contract on Bitcoin in 2016. BitMEX itself closed in September 2026, but the product it pioneered has become the most traded instrument in crypto.

Sources indicate that A perpetual contract never actually involves owning the asset. Traders deposit collateral, or "margin," and their profit or loss depends entirely on how the price moves.

Sources indicate that when opening a perp position, a trader chooses a direction. Going long means betting the price will rise; going short means betting it will fall. Being able to short as easily as going long is one reason perps are popular: it lets traders profit from falling prices, or hedge assets they already own.

Perps are usually traded with leverage, which lets traders control a larger position than their collateral alone would allow. With 10x leverage, for example, $100 of margin controls a $1,000 position. If the asset's price rises 5%, the trader makes $50, a 50% return on their margin. But if it falls 5%, they lose $50, half of their margin.

Sources indicate that exchanges track two prices to manage this. The index price is the asset's price on spot markets, usually averaged across several exchanges. The mark price, based on the index and the perp market itself, is used to calculate profits and losses and to decide when positions must be closed. Using an averaged price makes it harder for a sudden spike on one exchange to trigger liquidations.

According to recent reports, because perps never expire, nothing forces their price to converge with the underlying asset, as traditional futures do at expiry. Instead, perps use a funding rate.

At regular intervals—most commonly every eight hours, though some platforms use shorter or longer schedules—traders on one side of the market pay traders on the other:.

Decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, for example, pays funding every hour, at one-eighth of the rate calculated for an eight-hour period, to stay consistent with centralized exchanges.

Funding payments go directly between traders, not to the exchange. For traders holding positions over long periods, these payments can add up, and they can either boost or erode returns.

According to recent reports, funding rates also offer a window into market sentiment. Strongly positive funding suggests traders are crowded into bullish bets, while negative funding reveals that bears are paying to stay short.

Rates for the same asset can also differ between exchanges. On November 19, 2026, Bitcoin's funding rate was 0.01% per eight hours on Hyperliquid, compared with 0.0037% on Binance, according to Hyperliquid's funding comparison tool.

Recent findings suggest that some traders aim to earn funding payments rather than bet on prices. In a "cash and carry" or basis trade, they buy an asset on the spot market and short the same amount through perps, collecting funding while their positions offset each other's price moves.

In a recent development, leverage is a double-edged sword. Every perp position has a maintenance margin, the minimum collateral needed to keep it open. If losses push a trader's margin below that level, the exchange automatically closes the position, a process called liquidation. The trader typically loses most or all of the margin they put up.

Sources indicate that the higher the leverage, the smaller the price move needed to trigger a liquidation. At 50x leverage, a 2% move against a position can wipe it out.

Liquidations can also feed on each other. When prices fall sharply, liquidated longs are forced to sell, pushing prices lower and triggering further liquidations, a so-called liquidation cascade. On October 10, 2025, the crypto market saw its largest liquidation event on record, with more than $19 billion in leveraged positions wiped out in a single day.

It has been revealed that to cover losses when positions can't be closed in time, exchanges typically keep an insurance fund. In extreme cases, some use auto-deleveraging, closing profitable positions on the other side of the market to keep the system solvent.

Crypto perps trade on two main types of venue.

Centralized exchanges, such as Binance, Bybit and OKX, run their own order books and hold users' funds. They account for the vast majority of perps trading: Binance alone held about a third of centralized perps volume in early 2026, according to CoinGecko. Many are unavailable to U.S. customers.

Decentralized exchanges let traders use perps through smart contracts, while keeping control of their funds. Some, such as Hyperliquid and Solana-based Phoenix, run order books onchain, matching buyers and sellers much like a traditional exchange. Others, such as GMX and Jupiter, let traders trade against a shared pool of liquidity provided by other people.

Decentralized perps are growing fast. Their trading volume jumped from $1.5 trillion in 2024 to $6.38 trillion in 2025, led by Hyperliquid, CoinGecko found. Decentralized exchanges' share of perps trading volume peaked at 13% in late 2025 before slipping to 10% in April 2026, while their share of open interest, the total value of open positions, reached 13.5%.

It has been revealed that in the U.S., perps developed largely on offshore exchanges, outside the reach of the CFTC, but that has started to change. In July 2025, Coinbase introduced CFTC-regulated "perpetual-style" futures for U.S. customers, with five-year expiries and up to 10x leverage. Two months later, CFTC-regulated exchange Bitnomial introduced what it called the first U.S. perpetual futures, with 25-year terms and eight-hour funding. In May 2026, the CFTC approved a Bitcoin perpetual futures contract from prediction market Kalshi and set out a framework for listing more, and in June, Kraken rolled out perps to eligible U.S. customers through Bitnomial, which its parent company had acquired.

It has been revealed that some of these contracts, including Kalshi's and Bitnomial's original design, have long but fixed terms of 25 years, so are not strictly perpetual. The regulator says perps can be offered on CFTC-registered exchanges under federal oversight, and has advised U.S. traders to avoid offshore venues.

The shift has been contested. CME Group, the largest U.S. futures exchange, has sued the CFTC, arguing that perps are swaps rather than futures under U.S. law. The CFTC has nonetheless continued to approve more perps platforms, starting with Backpack.

It has been revealed that perps are now spreading beyond crypto. Exchanges have begun listing perps tracking stocks, stock indexes, commodities such as gold and oil, and currencies, giving traders around-the-clock exposure to markets that normally close in the evening and on weekends.

Sources indicate that those products carry the same mechanics, and the same risks, as crypto perps. They track an asset's price without giving traders ownership of the asset itself, so a perp on a firm's stock doesn't come with voting rights or dividends.

Perps can be useful tools for hedging and speculation, but they are among the riskiest products in crypto:.

In a recent development, decrypt users can now trade perps directly alongside the news, through the Decrypt Money Account. The service is powered by Phoenix, a decentralized exchange on Solana, and lets users go long or short on crypto, stocks and commodities.

Availability varies by region, and as with any leveraged product, traders should only risk money they can afford to lose.

Decrypt offers perpetual futures trading through the Decrypt Money Account, powered by Phoenix.

Tesla’s China sales crash 66% to lowest level in over four years

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, only 8,817 of the cars Tesla delivered from Giga Shanghai in October went to Chinese buyers.
  • Back in July 2022, the Shanghai factory was partly shut down for line upgrades.
  • The China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) reported that Tesla China wholesaled 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.3% year-over-year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, only 8,817 of the cars Tesla delivered from Giga Shanghai in October went to Chinese buyers. That’s down 66% from a year ago and Tesla’s worst month in China since July 2022, according to CPCA data.

Back in July 2022, the Shanghai factory was partly shut down for line upgrades. This time it ran normally and shipped 87% of what it built out of the country.

The China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) reported that Tesla China wholesaled 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.3% year-over-year. That’s the number most headlines ran with.

But 59,012 of those were exports. Strip them out and you’re left with 8,817 cars for the domestic market, the one Giga Shanghai was originally built to serve.

Sources indicate that nearly all of them were Model Ys (7,807), according to CnEVPost, leaving just 1,010 Model 3s. And compared to September, when Tesla sold 64,837 cars in China, domestic sales fell 86%.

Here’s how October has looked over the last three years:.

Tesla favors export orders early in each quarter and pushes domestic deliveries toward the end of it, and September’s promotions and quarter-end rush pulled some demand forward.

That’s real. Tesla’s China sales have followed this sawtooth pattern for years. Last October was also weak, and Tesla then delivered 73,145 cars in China in November and 93,843 in December.

But it doesn’t explain the size of this drop. Here’s every first month of a quarter in 2026:.

Sources indicate that october is less than half of the previous low this year. And the October trough keeps getting deeper: 40,485 in 2024, 26,006 in 2025, 8,817 now.

In a recent development, china’s EV market is having a rough year. NEV retail sales fell 10% year-over-year in October to 1.148 million units, according to CPCA’s preliminary data, as Beijing phases out trade-in subsidies and the NEV purchase tax exemption was cut in half on January 1. The overall passenger car market was down 25%.

In a recent development, tesla was down 66%. That works out to about 0.8% of China’s NEV retail market last month.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Xiaomi, which only started delivering cars in 2024, delivered more than 50,000 vehicles in October. Leapmotor delivered 106,127, up 51%. BYD delivered 490,168, though that includes its exports.

Through October, Tesla has sold 389,905 cars in China. That’s down 15% from 458,710 over the same period last year and its lowest January-to-October total in at least four years:.

The decline is speeding up. Tesla was down 11.9% in China through September, and one bad October pushed that to 15%. This year is now 22% below the 2024 peak, or about 110,000 fewer cars.

Exports from Giga Shanghai went the other way, up 101% to 420,984.

In a recent development, so this year, Shanghai has now shipped more cars abroad than it sold at home. Last year, domestic sales beat exports by more than two to one.

As we reported last month, Beijing is cutting the VAT export rebate on EVs from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027, with the rate set by the customs declaration date. We noted to expect automakers to cram exports in ahead of the deadline. October’s 59,012 exports, up 66% year-over-year, fit that.

Industry observers note that we’ve been tracking this gap all year, from Tesla’s Q1 China retail crash to the first-half numbers. Every time, the wholesale headline looks fine and the domestic number underneath gets worse. October is the most extreme version yet: Tesla China “grew” 10% while Chinese buyers bought 66% fewer Teslas.

In a recent development, we don’t buy that this is just the quarterly cycle. The cycle explains why October is weaker than September. It doesn’t explain why this October is a third of last October, or less than half of any other month this year.

I've been saying this for the last two years. Tesla's problem isn't that Elon temporarily alienated customers in Europe or other countries. Yes that killed sales for a bit, but in the end people are practical and will buy the best car for the money. And we saw that is exactly what happened with European Tesla sales coming back when gas prices rose and Tesla as a package (quality + price) was still very competitive.

In a recent development, the real problem that Tesla has is that they're falling behind in China not because anyone cares about Elon's politics, but because the cars are just less and less competitive. And while the Chinese competition doubles down on vehicle development and rolls out a upcoming car every week, Tesla has lost all interest in it. There is absolutely nothing on the horizon for them in terms of new vehicles that consumers can buy. Looks like the 3 and Y are all they will have and no updates are coming.

I know, FSD or bust, but that's also assuming Chinese brands don't crack that nut at the same time.

Sources indicate that two things can be true at once. The export numbers show Tesla front-loading shipments ahead of the rebate cut. And Chinese demand for a Model 3 and Model Y lineup that hasn’t fundamentally changed in years keeps fading while Xiaomi, Leapmotor and BYD launch latest models every few months.

And if Tesla is choosing to send cars abroad instead of selling them in China, that’s not exactly a vote of confidence in its Chinese business either.

The real test is November and December. Last year, Tesla bounced back to 73,000 and 94,000 domestic sales. If it gets close to that again, October was mostly timing. If it doesn’t, Tesla has a serious problem in the world’s largest EV market, and the export valve that’s been hiding it gets more expensive in April.

With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s not just you—everyone really is starting to work out lately. My feed is full of people hitting the weights for the first time ever or setting significant goals like getting their first pull-up. And let me just say: It’s awesome!

Sources indicate that so, if that’s you, let me officially say welcome to the party. When you’re starting to work out, it can be hard to sift through all the options and find a program that’s actually accessible for a true beginner (or, someone restarting after quite some time). That is, until now.

The Women’s Health+ 4-Week Beginner Workout Initiative takes the guesswork out of starting your fitness journey. This comprehensive program guides you through strength and cardio workouts that only take between 20 and 45 minutes. And, of course, it answers every burning question you could have about starting a fitness routine.

In a recent development, no matter your age or experience, starting an exercise routine has many benefits, states Kristen McParland, CPT, your coach for the next four weeks. Building muscle increases total-body strength; your bones, ligaments, and tendons get healthier; and even your blood pressure and immunity may improve. So lace up those sneakers and we’ll see you at the gym now, too.

Download the WH+ 4-Week Beginner Workout Initiative.

According to recent reports, over the next four weeks, you’ll follow a specific strategy each day, focusing either on strength training, optional cardio, active recovery, or rest (more on these, below). Each strength workout includes a warm-up and a cooldown (which you can use on cardio days, too). More info on each below.

Simply follow the instructions of each full-body strength training workout in the Women's Health+ Beginner Workout Initiative. You can find detailed how-to instructions for each exercise in the Exercise Guide section of the PDF.

Equipment Needed: Dumbbells, kettlebells, a step or box, and a slam ball. Don’t have access to a kettlebell or slam ball? Don't worry—you can still do those exercises with a dumbbell.

According to recent reports, cardio is vital for everyone, regardless of fitness level or routine. That’s because when you’re lifting heavy, your heart needs to be able to take on that stress. Training cardio—through running, cycling, or brisk walking—will help improve your heart strength.

If you’re a beginner when it comes to cardio, simply start at your own pace and build. Complete 20 to 30 minutes of running, biking, cycling, rowing, or using the elliptical or stair climber (whatever you enjoy). No matter which form of cardio you choose, start with interval training: exert yourself for 30 seconds, then go at a light pace for 1 to 2 minutes, alternating the pattern for a total of 20 minutes. The goal is to “get your heart rate up, but then pull it back and recover,” McParland says. Eventually, you’ll be able to decrease the rest time and maintain that higher-intensity movement for 15 to 20 minutes without a break.

In a recent development, your activity on this day is up to you. The goal is to do some kind of low-intensity movement lasting 20 minutes. Some ideas: outdoor walk or hike, bike ride, incline treadmill walk, yoga, or Pilates class.

Take this day to relax so your muscles have time to repair. Still, if your body is craving some type of activity for recovery, you could stretch, go for a walk, or even try a treatment like a massage, sauna, or cold-plunge session.

Here’s how things will progress each week.

Complete the five programmed workouts when it’s convenient for you. Focus on your form and take your two rest days when you need to recover.

If you completed all the workouts in Week 1, repeat them during Week 2, adjusting one variable in your routine, McParland claims: the number of reps or sets, the weight, the speed of the moves (slower is harder). If you missed a workout, don’t stress. Refocus on completing all of the Week 1 workouts before making any of the changes above.

You’ve officially done two full weeks of this workout plan—nice job! During this third week, repeat the workouts from Week 2 in exactly the same way or adjust one variable again (reps or sets, weight, range of motion, speed, and rest periods). If you feel you’re crushing it and are ready to level up, try the third full-body strength workout.

Industry observers note that still going strong? Thought so! Hit all six workouts and adjust one variable per workout for an extra challenge (reps or sets, weight, range of motion, speed, rest time). You can also ramp up your cardio time (to 30 to 40 minutes) or speed, shorten rest intervals (for interval training), or raise your step goal by 10 percent (e.g., if your daily step goal was 5,000 a day, make it 5,500).

Ready to become your strongest self? Download the WH+ 4-Week Beginner Workout Strategy now.

When you’re just beginning to work out, do a minimum of two full-body strength training days each week, McParland recommends. During both of those days, you should hit at least one exercise from each category of the foundational movement patterns. This will give you enough of a challenge to stimulate muscle growth, she says.

During the first two weeks of this plan, you will have two strength training days per week (each session will run 36 to 43 minutes), two optional cardio/step days per week (each session will 20 to 30 minutes), one day of active rest (a stint of low-intensity movement lasting at least 20 minutes), and two recovery days, for a total of five workouts per week.

Recent findings suggest that after those two weeks, see how your body feels and if your body is craving a third day of full-body training. If so, progress to the next phase of this strategy. That weekly schedule consists of three strength training days per week (each session will run 36 to 43 minutes), two optional cardio/step days per week (each session will run 20 to 30 minutes), one active rest day (lasting at least 20 minutes), and one recovery day, for a total of six workouts per week. If your body isn’t ready for three strength-training days yet, wait another two weeks. Once you’ve completed the full four weeks of this plan, consider adding in the third day.

What kind of weights should I choose?

In a recent development, start with medium weights that will challenge you for 10 to 12 reps, indicates Sariya. Essentially, you’ll want to feel you’ve reached 70 to 80 percent of your rate of perceived exertion (i.e., your fatigue level is at a 7 or 8 out of 10) by the time you’re doing your final reps in a set. When you feel you can do more than 12 reps, it’s time to increase your weight, but keep the same number of reps. This way, you’re always working toward your goal of building strength.

As for how much to increase by: a good rule of thumb is 2.5 to 5 pounds for an upper-body exercise and 5 to 10 pounds for a lower-body move.

What if I need to rest in the middle of a set?

Resting during a workout is key—if you don’t take enough time to recover between exercises, you won’t have enough energy in your body for the next one. With this plan, you’ll rest between moves in a superset or tri-set for 20 to 30 seconds, or however long it takes to transition between exercises. Between supersets and tri-sets, you’ll rest for one minute.

If you get fatigued in the middle of a set, push through if you feel safe doing so, Sariya states. However, if you feel dizzy or fear you might drop a weight on yourself, put it down and take time to recover. When you’re feeling better, you can start again. If you’re in any sort of pain, stop the workout entirely.

What kind of cardio should I do?

Industry observers note that cardio is a great supplement to strength training, McParland states. Plus, it has a slew of benefits, such as better endurance in strength training, better blood pressure regulation, and higher VO2 max, she says.

If you’re a beginner when it comes to cardio, simply start at your own pace and build. Pick any form of cardio you enjoy, whether that’s brisk walking, running, cycling, or swimming, and sprinkle it in two or three days a week for 20 to 30 minutes, McParland recommends.

What should I do on recovery days?

According to recent reports, on an active rest day, you’ll still exercise a bit through low-intensity movement, like a leisurely bike ride or hike. On a recovery day, you’ll do just that: recover. After all, you need to give your muscles time to rebuild and repair, Sariya indicates. But to maximize the recovery aspect, you can also opt to stretch, go for a gentle walk, or even get a self-care body treatment like a massage.

Once you’ve got the WH+ Beginner Workout Plan under your belt, you’re ready to take things to another level. One way to do that is by simply restarting the program—and completing the moves with heavier weights this time. (This is called progressive overload, and it’s another foundational concept in strength training. The idea is that over time, you will keep increasing the stimulus to your muscles to continuously challenge them and make them stronger.).

Picking the right weight is an art as much as it is a science, but for a general rule of thumb, for upper-body moves, increase your weights by 2.5 to 5 pounds and see how that feels. For lower-body ones, try adding 5 to 10. You should feel like you’re ending each set two to three reps away from failure (where your form starts to break down). You can tell you’re close if your range of motion starts to shorten or your reps are slowing down. That’s how you know you’re successfully challenging yourself. And, if you don’t happen to have a lot of different-sized weights at your disposal, you can always just increase the number of reps you do instead.

But, if you’re looking for something latest, WH+ has a bunch of other trainer-created programs to help you grow your knowledge and confidence in the gym and attack other fitness goals.

If you’re getting into working out from the bone density perks...

Try the WH+ 4 Weeks to Stronger Bones Plan.

If you’re on a body recomposition journey...

Try the WH+ Build & Burn Series.

Try the WH+ Strong After 50 Program.

If your goals are more glute-specific...

Try the WH+ Glute Gains Challenge.

Industry observers note that the withdrawal figure is a point-in-time reading. The diagram reveals possible inflows without estimating their timing or amount.

When nearly all of the pool is already lent out, a holder may have to wait for more USDS to come in before redeeming their full position.

Sources indicate that sky says the module has no mechanism to liquidate borrowers early to free up funds for depositors. The loan collateral is in SKY, while holders redeem their stUSDS shares for USDS available in the vault.

Sources indicate that sky Frontier Foundation separately remarked on Nov. 20 that users exchanged more than $2 billion of USDS for USDC the previous day through Sky’s Peg Stability Module. Sources indicate that the swap facility serves customers who already have USDS to exchange. An stUSDS holder using the vault would first have to redeem for USDS before using that route to get USDC.

The amount a vault depositor can withdraw depends on how much USDS is in the lending pool when the redemption is attempted.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Whitby Morrison bills itself as “the world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer,” supplying converted vans as ice cream trucks to drivers worldwide.
  • And now it has taken a big step into the modern age delivering its first fully electric ice cream truck to Hocking’s dairy in North Devon, England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The “world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer” has released its first fully electric ice cream truck, which is already in operaiton, and it claims it’s open for orders for more.

Whitby Morrison bills itself as “the world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer,” supplying converted vans as ice cream trucks to drivers worldwide.

And now it has taken a big step into the modern age delivering its first fully electric ice cream truck to Hocking’s dairy in North Devon, England.

The truck has been operating since July, through the course of one “ice cream season.” It reportedly covered more than 100 miles a day and has done days serving up to 12 hours at a time.

It has been revealed that it’s built on a standard Mercedes eSprinter, so it’s not retrofitted from the diesel vans that make up most of Whitby Morrison’s other offerings. The eSprinter comes in a “chassis cab” configuration which comes with just the chassis and cab, and lets upfitters build whatever they want onto the back end of the vehicle.

In this case, it also got some pretty extensive (and a little over-the-top) art all around the vehicle, highlighting the van’s electric operation.

The ice cream truck maker, Whitby Morrison, indicates this is the “world’s first fully certified electric ice cream truck.”.

We’re not sure what sort of international certifications are required for an ice cream truck so we’ll take their word for it, but we have seen a Rivian EDV turned into a Ben & Jerry’s ice cream truck, complete with side window, and a concept electric ice cream truck as far back as 2019. So it’s certainly not the very first time this idea has been had, at least.

And it is a good idea. As with school buses, ice cream trucks are vehicles that children are likely to congregate around. Having a stinky old truck spewing emissions just a few feet away from those kids’ lungs is the sort of thing that can expose them to a life of health problems… and we might as well not stack that on top of the sugar addiction we’re teaching them to have (hey, at least they have to get outside to chase the truck down, so they’re getting some physical activity out of it, right?).

It also opens up more possibilities for operators to serve at events where having a diesel truck running might not be reasonable, like in enclosed spaces or where quiet might be appreciated (this came up when we went to Harbinger Motors’ factory opening, where local food trucks were in attendance, inside the large factory building, and made the air quality noticeably worse).

Industry observers note that whitby Morrison says it’s taking orders both in the UK and overseas, with US orders just opening. To learn more, head on over to its website.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I REMEMBER THE first time I became aware of it.
  • New Coke was a thing people cared about.
  • Industry observers note that I was nine years old.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I REMEMBER THE first time I became aware of it. Or should I say lack of it.

I grew up in the mid '80s. A magical time. MTV actually played music videos. New Coke was a thing people cared about. And a ginger-headed German teenager named Boris Becker—Boom-Boom, to his millions of fans—became, at age 17, the youngest player ever to win Wimbledon.

Industry observers note that I was nine years old. And obsessed.

Industry observers note that while other kids my age were collecting Garbage Pail Kids cards or trying to solve Rubik’s Cubes, I was rewatching VHS recordings of Becker’s matches. I practiced his signature serve motion in front of my bedroom mirror. I begged—actually begged—my parents for the complete Boris Becker starter kit: the Ellesse tennis outfit, the Puma half-top sneakers, and the holy grail itself: the Puma Super tennis racket.

Industry observers note that the problem was, no matter how hard I tried, no matter how much Hi-C I consumed, I could never quite achieve the same explosive spring that made Boom-Boom so spectacular. Then I noticed something about Becker’s serve—the one that earned him his nickname. Most players bent their knees to generate power. Becker did something else.

He stuck out his butt. Like, really stuck it out. His serve motion involved this pronounced posterior thrust that helped him achieve that devastating topspin and pace.

I went to the bedroom mirror. Turned sideways. Attempted the same motion. And that’s when it hit me with all the force of one of Becker’s 130-mph serves: I didn’t have a butt to stick out. Where Becker had curvature, I had...continuity. My back just sort of continued into my legs.

Reality set in. No bum-bum, no boom-boom.

In a recent development, by high school, I had pivoted to more cerebral pursuits like creative writing and a burgeoning interest in art history. Art history seemed safe—just looking at old paintings and Roman sculptures, right? Wrong. It became immediately clear that every civilization in human history had one thing in common: great asses.

One fateful morning during my sophomore year, I was standing at my locker wearing a pair of saggy-bottomed Gap khakis when I heard giggles behind me. The distinctive sound of teenage girls discovering something hilarious and vaguely cruel.

According to recent reports, “Oh my God,” one of them said. I froze.

It has been revealed that “He has no butt!” another voice announced with the confidence of a scientist making a groundbreaking discovery. More giggling. Then came the death blow that would echo through the halls of my high school for the next two and a half years:.

It has been revealed that sure, it wasn’t the most creative nickname, but it had just enough alliteration to spread like a pre-internet meme. From that day on, I knew “they” knew.

I RECENTLY TURNED 50. I’m happily married and have two amazing kids. Life is good, but I’d be lying if I said the ghost of No-Butt Bender doesn’t haunt me. As I’ve aged, what little I had has somehow continued to erode. My wife loves me despite my anatomical deficiency but remains perpetually baffled by the lack of rear topography. And what was once giggles from teenage girls is now full-throated hysterical laughter from my 13- and 11-year-old children when they catch a glimpse of me in anything form-fitting.

According to recent reports, recently, Instagram’s insecurity algorithm served me up an ad for Perk men’s clothing. Their website is a gallery of flattering middle-aged bum-shots, but what really stopped my scroll was the pitch for their pants: “Our chinos magically turn even a flat butt into a compliment magnet. Whether you’re 25 or 65, that never gets old!”.

You have to understand—when you have no butt, no pants are flattering. So when Perk starts advertising pants that promise to be so bootylicious you’ll receive compliments everywhere you go, I dared to dream. I did what any man starved for posterior validation does—panic-ordered chinos in every damn color.

In a recent development, five pairs. Overnight shipping.

It has been revealed that the moment the package arrived, I tore it open. I slipped them on, turned toward the mirror, and—holy hell—was that…something? An actual curve? A protrusion? I squinted. I turned. And I practically sprinted to the living room where the family was waiting and struck a pose.

In a recent development, crickets. Then a full collapse into hysterical laughter.

“I’m sorry,” my wife gasped between laughs, “but those pants are working so hard and getting nowhere.”.

It has been revealed that I was tired of feeling like the only person other than Hank Hill to be cursed with diminished gluteal syndrome (DGS). It’s a very isolating condition. But I figured if Perk could build an entire organization around flat-figured men, there had to be others out there, living their lives in quiet resignation.

Close to midnight on a Wednesday, my face lit only by the glow of my computer, I did the obvious: Googled “men with no butts.”.

Industry observers note that the search results led me to a Reddit post titled, “Gentlemen, how do you live with having no butt?” This guy laid it all out: approaching 29, finally accepting his glute-free reality, enduring constant jokes from his girlfriend, the whole nine yards of tush-less trauma. But what really got me was his closing line: “Please help.”.

It has been revealed that I stared at those two words. They contained decades of my own experience—the loneliness, the confusion, the desperation. This post was five years old, but I didn’t care. I had to reach out.

In a recent development, I woke the following morning to find his response waiting like a message from a long-lost brother: “You seem legit I guess. Sure why not.” We were already bonding!

I asked Ross (names have been changed to protect the in-ass-cent) what motivated him to publicly post about his crisis on Reddit, and he said, “It was a genuine problem and if someone’s got an answer that helps, I was going to be all ears.”.

It has been revealed that ross first became aware of his DGS when a friend at the gym dropped the bomb: “Dude, you have no ass whatsoever.” The keen observation sent Ross into a spiral of photographic evidence review. He started examining pictures of himself and came to the only possible conclusion: “Huh, I guess I don’t.” It was his own bedroom-mirror moment.

Recent findings suggest that as for the wisdom he received from the Reddit hivemind, he noted it was mostly people prescribing the usual suspects: sprints and squats: “I was doing a shit ton of those back then and still do,” he told me. Still, Ross gave me the faintest glimmer that improvement was possible. Maybe a guy with no butt could transform it into a bona fide ba-donk-a-donk.

I phoned two lifelines from my past—Jonathan Botts, MD, a college friend who’d become an orthopedic surgeon at the Los Angeles Orthopedic Institute in Sherman Oaks, California, and Derek DeGrazio, Britney Spears’s former physical trainer, who had whipped me into the best shape of my life for my long-ago wedding and now is a partner at Barry’s Bootcamp Miami.

Sources indicate that when I asked about the possibility of maximizing my non-existus, he didn’t sugarcoat it. “Here’s the problem: You can’t go from what you are now to just working on your butt and developing a huge butt,” he told me. “People are doing lots of protein intake and protein shakes and bulking up like that. So basically, I’d need to become the Hulk to grow a butt.

Derek offered an alternate strategy with what he calls the Bender Big Three™. “I can’t say for certain, but I think No-Butt Bender can become Mild-Butt Bender with squats for foundation, Romanian deadlifts to pop your glute a little bit, and a nice hip thrust,” he noted.

Mild-Butt Bender. It did have a certain je ne sais quoi.

Recent findings suggest that derek, who freely admits he was born with “a great Italian ass,” is my gluteal bizarro from an alternate universe where only perfect butts exist. He told me his seat meat gave him confidence in high school, something I could only imagine by taping Springsteen’s Born in the USA album cover to the back of my pants. Derek played baseball, a sport notorious for its revealing tight pants. “I don’t know if they came to watch baseball or if they came to watch us in our uniforms,” he recalled, misty-eyed.

Sources indicate that I hated him. I loved him. I wanted to be him.

But then—plot twist!—just as I began fantasizing about playing shortstop, Derek dropped a bomb: “I started to realize that what was a blessing at one point became also my Achilles heel at the same time. If there is a downside, I wasn’t the fastest guy on the team.”.

In a recent development, wait. There was a downside to having a butt?

It has been revealed that dr. Botts, who describes his own posterior as “bigger than average,” delivered the final revelation: Having a bigger butt doesn’t automatically mean you have a stronger butt. “If you have a small butt, does that mean you have weak glutes? It doesn’t at all. You can have a significant butt and have really weak glutes.”.

All these years, I’d associated my small butt with weakness. With inadequacy. With being less than. What if I was wrong? What if, beneath my perpetually drooping pants lurked a superhero-strength posterior more powerful than even Derek’s celebrated Italian ass?

Industry observers note that unlikely. And who am I kidding? It’s not like if I had remarked to those girls in high school, “Oh no, you don’t understand—it’s really strong!” they would have stopped laughing and made out with me.

It has been revealed that but hey, this newly introduced knowledge gives me something to cling on to. Wish I could say the same for my pants. Still, I am what I am. I am No-Butt Bender. And if that makes my kids laugh and my wife give me a warm, “It’s okay. I love you anyway” hug, I’ll take it.

Variational raised $110 million and aims to use it to lift trading limits on Omni, its derivatives platform.

The manufacturer is recruiting more dealers as it expands into more stock, index, commodity, and currency markets. Omni traders will still rely on a single counterparty to pay their gains.

Bain Capital Crypto led the Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, Variational announced on Nov. 18. CEO Lucas Schuermann stated in the organization’s release that stocks, indexes and commodities already accounted for more than half of Omni’s daily volume.

According to recent reports, variational remarked that an unnamed tier-one market maker already supplies liquidity for swaps. It is seeking institutions that can quote equities, commodities and currencies around the clock.

In a recent development, the Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP) is Variational’s in-house market maker, which quotes a price and takes the other side when a customer trades. It can then hedge that exposure with a traditional dealer or on another venue.

More dealers can help OLP quote more markets and take on more exposure, but the customer still settles with OLP.

At 20:10 UTC on Nov. 20, Omni’s public market table demonstrated $94.6 million in open interest on the Nasdaq-100 swap and $57.1 million on the gold swap.

Industry observers note that variational had set the initial caps at about $10 million per market when the two swaps introduced in September. It said then it planned to lift each cap to $50 million or more. The company put potential capacity under its initial dealer agreements at more than $1 billion across the arrangements.

Under the standard schedule, both swaps trade from midnight to 5 p.m. and from 6 p.m. through 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on weekdays. They close on weekends, and holidays can change trading hours.

During a closure, orders and liquidations wait until the market reopens, while around-the-clock swap trading remains a goal.

In a recent development, variational reported over $1.3 billion in Omni open interest with the round. Entropy Advisors’ on-chain dashboard demonstrates a series that includes OLP alongside one that counts only traders’ positions. On its traditional-markets chart, OLP’s side equals the traders’ side.

According to recent reports, omni’s public API counts both sides in the platform total and counts only traders in its per-market long and short figures. The Series B release leaves its counting basis unspecified, so lining it up with the dashboard would require matching the series and the observation time.

Each Omni trader and OLP post collateral to a separate on-chain settlement pool for that pair, and a vault holds USDC to supply OLP’s margin.

OLP uses its own capital when hedging outside the platform, leaving customers’ collateral in their pools.

It has been revealed that traders settle with the Omni Liquidity Provider. OLP can hedge separately with dealers and other external venues.

In extreme volatility or a severe liquidity squeeze, OLP’s margin problem can force a trader’s position to close.

If OLP becomes insolvent, gains that accrue from then on can go unpaid, even if the trader has realized them.

The trader and OLP both post collateral to their shared on-chain pool. OLP owes the trader any gains.

Juiced unveils another lower-cost moto-styled electric bike: Scrambler Core

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a latest, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core.
  • The newly introduced Scrambler Core starts at $1,399, compared to $1,699 for the existing Scrambler Hardtail.
  • Juiced is also offering a $1,599 long-range version of the Core, as well as a smaller “Midsize” frame that should make the bike much more accessible to shorter riders – and, perhaps more importantly, teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a latest, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core. The new bike keeps much of the moto-inspired styling and performance of the existing Scrambler Hardtail, but trims back several components to knock several hundred dollars off the price.

The newly introduced Scrambler Core starts at $1,399, compared to $1,699 for the existing Scrambler Hardtail.

Juiced is also offering a $1,599 long-range version of the Core, as well as a smaller “Midsize” frame that should make the bike much more accessible to shorter riders – and, perhaps more importantly, teenagers.

Recent findings suggest that teens are a major part of the moto-style e-bike market, and Juiced has designed its Scrambler e-bikes as a safer option for those younger riders. In addition to ensuring street-legal performance for most major markets, Juiced rolled out a feature known as Speed Lock, which is essentially a parental control option that lets a parent or guardian set a lower speed limit using a PIN code that prevents their teen from later modifying the speed limit.

Sources indicate that the launch comes as part of the rebirth of Juiced Bikes following the brand’s acquisition last year. The company was founded in 2009 and was acquired in 2025 by the co-founders of Lectric Ebikes, who have since brought the brand back with a new generation of its popular Scrambler platform.

The biggest changes appear to be in the powertrain, battery, brakes, and suspension.

The standard Scrambler Hardtail launched earlier this year set the standard for the flagship models by using a 750W nominal motor with 90 Nm of torque and reaching 28 mph (45 km/h). Its 52V 19.2Ah battery provides nearly 1 kWh of capacity and a claimed range of up to 60 miles (96 km).

According to recent reports, the Scrambler Core steps down to a 500W nominal rear hub motor rated for 1,176W peak and 80 Nm of torque. Top speed is also reduced slightly to 25 mph (40 km/h), while the throttle is limited to 20 mph (32 km/h). Importantly, though, Juiced has retained its 52V architecture, meaning this is still a fairly punchy setup rather than a dramatically detuned budget bike.

Battery capacity takes a hit as well. The standard Core gets a 52V 10Ah battery with 520 Wh of capacity, rated for up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Spending another $200 gets the Core Long-Range with a 52V 15Ah, 780Wh battery and a claimed 60-mile (96 km) maximum range. As with nearly all e-bikes, expect real-world range to fall short of the idealized advertised numbers, which are generally only achievable under the lowest power pedal assist.

It has been revealed that juiced also traded the Talon P4 four-piston hydraulic brakes found on the more expensive Scrambler for Talon P2 two-piston brakes. The KKE inverted fork with 140mm of travel is gone too, replaced by a more conventional aluminum triple-crown fork with 100mm of travel.

Sources indicate that those are meaningful downgrades, but they’re also largely the kinds of changes I’d expect to see when trying to shave $300 off an already competitively priced moto-style e-bike. It’s a strategy we’ve seen play out before in the industry, helping lower costs for riders who want a flagship bike but don’t necessarily want to pay flagship prices.

Sources indicate that even so, crucial features remain to help maintain the look and feel of the Juiced Scrambler line. The Core still gets 20 x 4-inch fat tires, hydraulic disc brakes, a frame-integrated TFT display, four pedal-assist levels, a headlight, taillight, brake light, and turn signals. It’s a single-speed setup and weighs 73 lb (33 kg), while being rated for a 300 lb (136 kg) payload.

Perhaps the more interesting addition is the Scrambler Core Midsize.

While the regular Core is recommended for riders 5’2” and taller, the Midsize drops that figure to just 4’10”. Pricing remains the same: $1,399 with the 520Wh battery or $1,599 with the 780Wh long-range pack.

And with an eye towards safety, the Core and Core Mini retain Juiced’s PIN-protected parental speed lock. Parents can set the motor-assisted top speed anywhere from 1-25 mph and lock the setting behind a four-digit PIN. That makes even more sense on the Midsize version, which seems tailor-made for younger riders who want the moto-style look but may not yet comfortably fit the larger Scrambler.

Sources indicate that the Core is launching in several decidedly Juiced color names, including Black Nectar, Fruit Punch, Sour Grape, White Grape, Berry Freeze, and Blood Orange, though availability varies between frame sizes and battery configurations. Juiced states preorders are expected to begin shipping around the end of the month.

In a recent development, at $1,399, the Scrambler Core feels like a logical extension of Juiced’s rebooted lineup. You lose some battery, motor power, braking hardware, suspension travel, and a few mph compared to the Hardtail, but the underlying recipe is largely intact. For riders who mostly want the Scrambler look and feel – or parents shopping for a smaller rider – saving $300 may be a pretty compelling trade. Especially when you consider that the original Juiced Scrambler already led the industry in value for moto-style e-bikes from reputable brands.

Toss in the strong backing from Lectric and the 3-year warranty, and it’s hard to consider much else among the competition.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that you've seen enough GRWM videos to know that plenty of people are incorporating lymphatic drainage tools into their morning routines. If you also grapple with regular facial puffiness, it's fair to wonder if lymphatic drainage tools could help.

In a recent development, these tools are marketed to encourage the flow of lymph, which is a clear, watery fluid that supports fluid balance and immune defenses in your body. The idea with lymphatic drainage tools—which include gua sha stones, facial rollers, dry brushes, and more—is to mechanically encourage the movement of lymphatic fluid to reduce puffiness and fluid retention.

In a recent development, dermatologists say there's something to this. "Your lymph system helps move excess waste and fluid throughout the body," explains Joshua Zeichner, MD, director of cosmetic and clinical research at Mount Sinai Hospital. "Lymphatic massages help enhance activity of the system to circulate excess fluid and depuff.".

Doctors may recommend lymphatic drainage massage to people with health conditions like lymphedema or to post-surgical patients, notes Ife J. Rodney, MD, founding director of Eternal Dermatology + Aesthetics. For everyone else, the data is less clear on whether lymphatic drainage offers much benefit.

Industry observers note that "For everyday facial puffiness, gentle massage may offer temporary improvement, though research on gua sha is limited," Dr. Rodney claims. Note the "temporary" part of what she said. Despite what you may hear on social media, lymphatic drainage won't permanently alter your cheekbones and jawline, although Dr. Rodney says this may help your skin look fresher and your features look more defined. "Think of it as an optional self-care step, not a requirement for healthy skin," Dr. Rodney says.

Want to opt into this? There is a range of tools to consider—and doctors say you don't need to spend a ton to get results.

A gua sha tool needs to have at least one smooth edge for lymphatic drainage. But Face Gym's Multi-Sculpt High-Performance Contouring Tool has six different edges to focus on different areas of your face. Long and medium smooth edges are made for classic lymphatic drainage, while shorter sides are ideal for areas around your eyes. The tool even includes rounded teeth for fine lines and a targeted tip for acupressure. (Face Gym has an instructional video to help guide you through all of this.).

Sources indicate that face Gym's gua sha tool is made from stainless steel, which is hypoallergenic and easy to clean. The stainless-steel tool is easy to clean, but any product can irritate skin. It also has a nice cooling effect after briefly popping it into the fridge. While this gua sha tool is on the pricier end, its stainless steel construction means it won't shatter like its crystal counterparts if you accidentally drop it.

Industry observers note that both are used for facial massage, but a roller moves across the skin by rolling, while gua sha uses sweeping strokes with a smooth-edged tool. You simply glide the roller across your face with gentle pressure to support lymphatic drainage. This is another stainless steel tool, which means it's a little more hygienic and easy to clean than its more traditional crystal versions. It's also highly likely to survive in the event of a drop.

The stainless steel has a natural cooling feel against the skin, although you can toss it in the fridge for extra chilliness. This tool is heavier than stone or crystal rollers—keep that on the back burner if you're used to those. It also pairs best with an oil or serum to help it glide smoothly over your skin, so strategy to moisturize at the same time.

Dry brushing has the combined benefit of supporting lymphatic drainage and exfoliation at once. But some brushes have stiff bristles that can feel intense—and even irritating—against the skin. Esker's dry brush is gentle against the skin, but still feels firm enough to get things moving.

Esker's dry brush has a spa-like feel, along with an ergonomic design that's easy to grip. It's relatively petite, too, making it easy to toss in a bag for travel or trips to the gym. The only downside of that is the handle isn't long enough to reach your back. (That's more of an exfoliation issue vs. a lymphatic drainage problem, though.) The rules of lymphatic drainage still apply with a brush like this—if it feels irritating to your skin, stop. But if dry brushing is something you're into and you want to try lymphatic drainage on areas of your body other than your face, this is a solid choice.

Most people do gua sha on their face with a sculpting stone, crystal, or steel device. But not everyone is into the sensation of moving something hard across the sensitive skin in that area. Skin Gym answers the call with a face brush designed specifically for gua sha.

The brush is densely packed with soft bristles, creating a feel like you're swiping a really good makeup brush over your skin. It has an ergonomic shape, making it easy to glide over the contours of your face. This brush is pretty beginner-friendly, making it a good entry point if you're gua sha-curious. But be aware that you may not be able to get as much pressure on your skin (if that's even your thing) as you would with a stone or other hard tool. The brush also requires regular cleaning to avoid pushing dirt around your face.

Let's get this out of the way upfront: Vibration plates are a controversial tool. Many make bold claims, like that they can support weight loss or mimic the effects of exercise—those are unfounded. But these plates can improve circulation and lymphatic drainage as a result, as Rachelle Reed, PhD, an exercise scientist based in Athens, Georgia, previously told Women's Health.

FWIW, research suggests that you'll get many of the same circulation- (and lymph-)promoting effects from exercise. But if a vibrating plate is more your speed, the LifePro Waver is worth a look. This machine offers 99 speed levels to allow you to fine-tune the intensity. The motor is also quiet, so you don't have to stress about waking up other people in your home. This plate comes with resistance bands and free online workout videos, too. Just be aware that vibration plates aren't safe for everyone—you should take a pass if you're pregnant, prone to blood clots, or struggle with dizziness, for example. Bachelorette star Gabby Windey also recently shared that she broke her back after cranking up her (unnamed) vibrating plate in the name of lymphatic drainage. Though her account is an individual anecdote and doesn’t establish the typical risk, proceed with caution. But if you're looking for a way to get lymphatic drainage moving around your whole body, this is worth considering.

Recent findings suggest that the best type of lymphatic drainage tool for you depends on where you proposal to use it on your body. "These types of massages can be performed anywhere, but are extremely common on the face," Dr. Zeichner notes. "Oftentimes, a smooth, but firm tool like gua sha is used.".

Industry observers note that A roller is another option for facial lymphatic drainage, and is usually considered more gentle than gua sha. For lymphatic drainage other than the face, some people reach for dry brushes and vibration plates.

In a recent development, for gua sha, Dr. Rodney suggests choosing a tool with smooth, rounded edges with no sharp spots, chips, or cracks. "It should be comfortable to hold and easy to clean," she claims—and that applies to all lymphatic drainage tools. For gua sha and rollers, "you don't need an expensive crystal," Dr. Rodney says.

Dry brushes should also have natural fibers, since synthetic can feel harsh against the skin. Overall, "a smooth finish and gentle technique matter more than the price tag," Dr. Rodney notes.

There's no exact weight for a lymphatic drainage tool that's best for everyone. Instead, it should feel substantial in your hand—but not too heavy or too light. You want to be able to comfortably use your tool, and allow the tool to apply pressure vs. heavy force from you.

They may temporarily reduce puffiness for some people, but evidence for at-home tools and broader health benefits is limited. "For everyday facial puffiness, gentle massage may offer temporary improvement," Dr. Rodney says. Dr. Zeichner agrees. "Especially if you wake up puffy in the morning after drinking too much alcohol, not having enough sleep, taking in too much salt, or during your menstrual cycle, lymphatic massages can be a useful tool," he says. Just keep in mind that the effects are temporary.

Every type of tool is slightly different. "The goal of a lymphatic massage is to improve the body's drainage system," Dr. Zeichner claims. "That is why the massage should be performed in a particular way." If you're massaging your face, the pressure should start near the center of your face, before moving out and down toward your collarbones. This follows the natural lymphatic flow, Dr. Zeichner says.

Industry observers note that "A few minutes is enough to start," Dr. Rodney says. "Keep the pressure light—bruising is a sign to stop, not a sign it’s working.".

In a recent development, dermatologists recommend taking a pass on lymphatic drainage tools if your skin is irritated, infected, sunburned, or broken. (That includes inflamed acne, eczema, or rosacea flares, per Dr. Rodney.).

Industry observers note that dr. Rodney also suggests checking with your doctor if you take blood thinners, bruise easily, or have blood clots, heart or kidney failure, lymphedema, or a history of cancer treatment or lymph node removal. "After cosmetic procedures or surgery, get clearance from your treating clinician," she claims. "Persistent or painful swelling needs an explanation before it needs a massage.".

💡 Key Takeaways
