  • I’M A SUCKER for a good Barbour jacket.
  • But as much as I love Barbour jackets, dropping several hundred dollars on one isn’t exactly in everyone’s budget.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

I’M A SUCKER for a good Barbour jacket. I’ve always considered the British heritage brand’s waxed-cotton outerwear the perfect finishing touch to a nicely put-together fall-winter outfit. Founded in 1894, Barbour originally made weather-resistant jackets for sailors, fishermen, and outdoor workers before becoming a staple of British countryside dressing. Over the years, its association with the royal family, including Princess Diana and King Charles III, helped give the rugged outerwear an upper-class appeal. But in the past five years, Barbour has seen a major resurgence, thanks to the barn-jacket boom on runways at Prada, Loewe, and Bottega Veneta, along with a growing appetite for timeless pieces over fast fashion. Buzzy collaborations with designers like Gucci and Paul Smith, plus the popularity of British countryside style in demonstrates like The Crown, have also introduced the look to a whole latest generation of guys.

But as much as I love Barbour jackets, dropping several hundred dollars on one isn’t exactly in everyone’s budget. Some of the brand’s most iconic styles, including the Bedale, Beaufort, and Ashby, will set you back anywhere from $415 to $450. And that’s before you dive into the designer collabs. Take the latest J.Crew x Barbour Beaufort jacket. It’s a fresh, reimagined take on the brand’s signature outerwear, dressed in a bold apple-green shade with a weather-resistant finish and tartan lining. Personally, it has me in a chokehold. At nearly $500, it’s a pretty steep investment, especially if you’re just looking to dip your toes into the barn-jacket trend.

Thankfully, you don’t have to spend that kind of money to capture the same British countryside charm. Plenty of menswear brands have put their own spin on the classic barn jacket, offering similar silhouettes, canvas fabrics, and utilitarian details at more digestible prices. I’ve rounded up some stylish Barbour jacket alternatives from brands like Bonobos and Quince that look just as sharp, whether you’re getting dressed up or keeping it casual.

Industry observers note that of all the Barbour jacket alternatives I’ve tested, Quince’s version comes close in comparison to the Barbour x Paul Smith collaboration I already own. That jacket runs north of $800, while Quince’s costs just over a hundred bucks but with nearly all the same bells and whistles: a two-tone brown colorway, contrasting corduroy collar, and snap-button storm throat flap that helps seal out drafts of wind. There’s also a two-way zipper that lets me open the jacket from the bottom when I need a little more breathing room.

It’s made from 100% organic cotton and fully lined with soft cotton flannel, which adds a welcome layer of warmth on chilly days when I can skip wearing a bulky sweater underneath. The cut hits just below the waist, with a roomy fit that leaves plenty of space for layering without feeling overly baggy. I’ve even worn it through a few light rain showers, and the fabric didn’t get soaked. I also appreciate how the classic design makes it easy to dress up with trousers and an Oxford shirt or keep things casual with jeans and boots.

In a recent development, uniqlo makes one of the best affordable Barbour alternatives I’ve come across, and at just $80, it looks and feels more expensive than it actually is. The lightly padded cotton-nylon fabric provides just enough warmth for temps below 60 degrees. What I especially like is the clean, sleek design that comes with a concealed front closure that hides the buttons and zipper, giving the jacket a sharper, more polished look when fully fastened. There’s also a classic checked lining and two-way flap pockets that can be accessed from the top or sides.

Fit-wise, it has a relaxed, boxy silhouette that hits right at the waist and leaves enough room to comfortably layer a chunky knit over a dress shirt. And unlike some barn jackets that lean heavily into the rugged workwear aesthetic, this one feels a little more understated. It comes in versatile neutrals like olive, khaki, black, and dark brown, so finding one that works with your wardrobe shouldn’t be difficult.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for something that puts a slightly different spin on the traditional barn jacket, Bonobos has you covered. Its Canvas Ranch Jacket trades the usual waxed-cotton construction for a sturdy cotton-elastane blend that has a little stretch, so I’m not feeling boxed in. But what really caught my attention are the angled patch pockets across the front. They’re a subtle departure from the usual straight-cut or flap pockets you see on most field jackets, giving the whole design a more distinctive, modern feel.

The cut extends past the waist and lands around the upper thigh, offering a little more coverage than your typical trucker jacket. I also like that Bonobos keeps the color options simple with midnight navy and forest green, both of which go nicely with denim, chinos, or tailored trousers.

For guys who want the classic Barbour look with a little more protection against the elements, consider this insulated version from L.L.Bean. Unlike some of the lighter options on this list, this one is packed with 60 grams of PrimaLoft Black insulation, a lightweight synthetic fill that helps keep it toasty inside without the bulk of a heavy winter coat. The 100% cotton exterior has a water-resistant waxed finish that will keep you dry in light rain. It also has a quilted exterior that gives the traditional field-jacket silhouette a slightly more outdoorsy vibe.

Industry observers note that it’s slightly fitted, so guys who are super jacked might have to size up. But the regular-length cut makes it easy to wear over everyday layers and not feel overly snug. This is a great option for construction laborers, landscapers, and other guys who spend long hours outdoors. It’s more practical than fashion-forward, but you get the timeless look of a heritage field jacket with added insulation and weather protection that make it useful beyond just completing an outfit.

Flint and Tinder’s waxed trucker jacket famously appeared on Pedro Pascal in HBO’s The Last of Us, and we’ve been major fans ever since. This is a burly, no-nonsense trucker jacket made from Martexin waxed sailcloth that’s treated on both sides to help block wind and repel light rain. The antique-finish metal buttons and earthy color options give it that rugged, worn-in look that only gets better with age. On the inside, a full-length blanket-style lining keeps you cozy during 50-degree mornings.

One thing worth mentioning is that the waxed fabric feels pretty stiff at first, so don’t expect it to have that soft, broken-in feel right out of the gate. But that’s also part of the appeal of this type of outerwear. After three wears, the fabric gradually softens and develops more character. Compared to Barbour’s longer field jackets, this one has a more traditional trucker silhouette, so I can pair it with jeans, boots, and other casual staples.

According to recent reports, not every Barbour alternative needs to look like it belongs in the English countryside. Case in point: AYR’s The Club, which takes a more refined approach. It’s made from weatherproofed waxed cotton that offers a water-repellent finish. The fabric is also light enough to wear across three seasons, making it a versatile option for those in-between days when a heavy coat feels like overkill.

Industry observers note that I can throw it over a tee with jeans for the weekend or wear it with a collared shirt and trousers to the office. I wore it in light showers, and it didn’t soak through to my clothes. And at a little over $300, it’s certainly not the cheapest alternative on this list. Still, if you’re after something that feels more stylish than rugged, this one makes a strong case for itself.

Ivy Shapiro's Manhattan Home is an Artful Ode to Old-School Newly introduced York

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1020 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Describing the allure of her sprawling prewar Manhattan apartment, art adviser Ivy Shapiro returns to one theme again and again.
  • Industry observers note that A Joel Shapiro sculpture holds a corner of the dining room beneath a painting by Aubrey Saget.
  • Recent findings suggest that in the living room, a painting by Cecily Brown hangs above a Joel Shapiro table with sculptures by Jonathan Borofsky (left) and Ivy Shapiro’s daughter, Lily Crewdson (right), beside a Southeast Asian sculpture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Describing the allure of her sprawling prewar Manhattan apartment, art adviser Ivy Shapiro returns to one theme again and again. “It’s old-school,” she insists. “I have this fantasy that I’m living in a different era. I wanted the apartment to capture this nostalgic vision of old-school Upcoming York elegance.” She had plenty to work with. The bones of the unit—its high ceilings, architectural details, and idiosyncratic layout of generous salons and small, meandering rooms—remained largely intact. Major structural alterations were unnecessary to make the space her own, a home that reflects her singular character while graciously accommodating an extensive collection of art that ranges from Stone Age tools and Southeast Asian antiquities to modern and contemporary works created by friends and family.

Industry observers note that A Joel Shapiro sculpture holds a corner of the dining room beneath a painting by Aubrey Saget. Works on paper by Edgar Degas and Bob Thompson surmount the fireplace, which is clad in black encaustic tile by clé.

Recent findings suggest that in the living room, a painting by Cecily Brown hangs above a Joel Shapiro table with sculptures by Jonathan Borofsky (left) and Ivy Shapiro’s daughter, Lily Crewdson (right), beside a Southeast Asian sculpture. A Jasper Johns lithograph hangs at rear. Sculpture in foreground by Tony Smith.

A Jeremy Anderson chandelier from Gallery Fumi crowns the makeup room. On the wall are works on paper by Cecily Brown.

Shapiro was born into the Latest York art world of the 1970s, when the artist and collector community had a far different complexion than that of today, a time before “the art world” meant “the art-fair world.” She is the daughter of the late celebrated sculptor Joel Shapiro and art educator Amy Snider, and the stepdaughter of artist Ellen Phelan. Hers is a life organized around and by art, so it is no surprise that the same would be true of her apartment. Here, art is offered the same sovereignty as the home’s human inhabitants, the freedom to take up space, require concessions, demand attention, and even, occasionally, to trip you up. It doesn’t have to fit in above a sofa or over a mantel, nor does it have to stand for something—taste, wealth, a movement, a generation. She accords each piece the independence to exist on its own terms, to be at home.

It has been revealed that “I like hanging art in weird places where people don’t like to hang,” Shapiro says. “It’s not an intellectual exercise. It’s more intuitive.”.

Recent findings suggest that architect Raffaella Bortoluzzi, Shapiro’s accomplice in the gentle transformation of the home, drew inspiration from her client’s unconventional sensibility. “I love that Ivy decided not to combine the small rooms and try to impose a more contemporary approach on how the spaces flow. We wanted to respect the historic character and maintain the eccentricities,” Bortoluzzi notes. “Our idea was that every room should have its own little story. We focused on light, playful treatments that in no way fight the original architecture.”.

Floating tiled shelves in the kitchen display ceramics by Warren MacKenzie and Shio Kusaka and a small sculpture by Joel Shapiro.

The television room features paintings by Lothar Hempel (left) and Elizabeth Murray (right).

A Joel Shapiro drawing has pride of place in the bedroom of Ivy Shapiro’s son, Walker Crewdson. To the right are a drawing by Sol LeWitt and a Joel Shapiro print.

In a recent development, the television room, for example, is enrobed in aubergine Venetian plaster. The home office, covered in a crimson plaster, features shelves and drawer fronts finished with a surface treatment of crushed eggshells encased in epoxy. Bortoluzzi goosed the primary bath by sprinkling a handful of Piero Fornasetti tiles among a field of pearlescent, zellige-like ones. In Shapiro’s makeup room, ladylike pink plaster walls are amplified by an antique mirror, custom shoe closets with floral fabric behind the glass case fronts, and a sprightly Jeremy Anderson chandelier. “Ivy is very funny and feminine in her way,” the architect states. “The design speaks to those aspects of her personality.”.

In the dining room, a Jean Arp collage is installed above an antique tansu with Stone Age tools and Joel Shapiro maquettes.

The last sculpture Joel Shapiro created rests on a table in the primary bedroom. The painting is by Bob Thompson. The sofa is covered in a Rubelli brocade.

Shelves and drawer fronts in the home office are covered in a surface material of crushed eggshells by Nature Squared.

Within the newly refurbished architectural shell, Shapiro deployed her estimable collection of art and objets de vertu with wit and verve. In the living room, the way that Jonathan Borofsky’s bronze Split Head sculpture is balanced by the split-off stone head of an Asian deity feels like a call and response across the ages, as well as a vignette about the endurance of art. They flank a dynamic painting by Shapiro’s friend Cecily Brown like chaperones at an orgy of color and motion. A sculpture by Shapiro’s daughter, Lily Crewdson, joins the Borofsky piece atop a table made by her father, one of many Joel Shapiro sculptures, drawings, and maquettes installed throughout the apartment.

A sculpture by Richard Artschwager is installed above a Joel Shapiro bronze in a hallway.

An Axel Salto sculpture sits beneath an artwork by Ryan Sullivan in the living room.

Sources indicate that in the hallway to the primary bedroom, a lyrical vintage Danish wall light of abstracted vines, leaves, and flowers hangs above a signature Carl Andre metal floor sculpture, the ultimate butch/femme pairing. In the bedroom itself, a sculpture that Joel Shapiro made in the hospital during his final days (he died in June of 2025) sits inconspicuously on a small table of his own design. It was the last artwork of his storied career.

It has been revealed that “Living with so much of Joel’s art, and all these amazing things he and Ellen collected, connects me to [my dad],” Shapiro muses. “The way the apartment is set up, I feel like my life is completely integrated with the art.”.

Garmin and Waze just teamed up on a clever new way to keep cyclists safer

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting newly introduced safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.
  • In a recent development, the new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature.
  • As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting newly introduced safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.

In a recent development, the new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature. That location can then appear in real time to nearby drivers using Waze, with cyclists displayed as moving icons on the road.

As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.

I’ve long maintained that safety – or more accurately, the perception that cycling isn’t safe – is one of the biggest impediments to getting more people onto bikes.

In a recent development, that’s especially true in the US, where cyclists are often forced to share roads with cars instead of enjoying the kind of widespread separated cycling infrastructure found in many more bike-friendly countries. And when a cyclist and a multi-ton vehicle have to occupy the same space, making sure the driver knows that cyclist is there can make a big difference.

Of course, an icon on Waze isn’t going to magically make cycling safe. It won’t replace protected bike lanes, better road design, slower vehicle speeds, or attentive drivers.

But I can certainly imagine situations where it could help. Riding at night or in poor visibility, approaching a blind curve, or simply traveling on a narrow road where a driver might otherwise come upon a cyclist unexpectedly are all situations where an advance warning could be useful.

Recent findings suggest that the feature is opt-in through Garmin Connect and activates when the cyclist starts an outdoor cycling activity. Garmin notes location sharing is temporary and session-based, and that cyclists’ personal information isn’t displayed in Waze. Of course, anyone who uses a personal GPS device has already accepted that their location is shared with Big Tech in exchange for features they value, but at least we know that any personalized info stays within Garmin instead of proliferating even further.

In a recent development, this is cool but requires both a Garmin product and the Waze app. IMHO better to equip latest cars and trucks with bicycle and pedestrian detection.

Garmin LiveTrack itself is free for users with compatible Garmin devices and previously allowed cyclists to share their live location, speed, route, and other information with friends and family. I’ve used it myself as a safety feature when venturing off-road and on longer solo journeys. The Waze integration essentially expands that safety net to nearby motorists.

There’s obviously one big limitation: You need to be riding with a compatible Garmin device, and the driver needs to be using Waze.

But with Waze claiming around 200 million users globally and Garmin being one of the biggest names in cycling computers and fitness watches, that’s not exactly a tiny Venn diagram.

Anything that gives drivers another chance to see cyclists before actually seeing them sounds like a win to me.

Binance can hold MEXC deposits even after the blockchain clears them

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • That's what Binance told customers to expect while it reviews deposits from MEXC.
  • The US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec.
  • MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

That's what Binance told customers to expect while it reviews deposits from MEXC. Try to move money the other way, and Binance says it'll refuse to send it in the first place.

The US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec. 10, but Binance announced its policy a month earlier and cited the Treasury's finding.

MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.

On Nov. 6, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) found that MEXC was a foreign financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.

The agency acted under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, and its order in the Federal Register prohibits transfers to and from MEXC through covered US financial institutions.

The prohibition has no scheduled end and covers MEXC's foreign operations and successor entities. It reaches crypto as well as conventional money, and FinCEN names Bitcoin explicitly.

Foreign financial firms can make dollar payments through banks that hold accounts with US banks, an arrangement known as correspondent banking.

FinCEN considered restricting those accounts but concluded that doing so would leave other kinds of transfers untouched. Instead, it chose to prohibit transfers that pass through a covered institution, even when MEXC has no account with the institution handling the payment.

Exchanges and payment providers outside that group may adopt their own restrictions, but those policies require separate confirmation.

Recent findings suggest that finCEN estimates that MEXC handled at least $16.7 billion in likely illicit activity in the five years through May 2026. The agency's figures include about $129 million it indicates MEXC directly facilitated with Garantex after the Russian crypto exchange was sanctioned, and about $4.1 million involving its successor, Grinex, after it too was sanctioned.

FinCEN also cites transfers linked to Iran and North Korea, along with proceeds from cybercrime. The agency acknowledges that legitimate customers use MEXC and says the financial risks it identified warrant restricting transfers involving the exchange itself.

Sources indicate that in its Nov. 7 public response, MEXC said it was operating normally, and customer assets remained secure. It said it had opened an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls and intended to engage with regulators.

Reports noted net outflows from tracked MEXC wallets after the announcement.

Binance can refuse to send a withdrawal because it controls the account the money would leave.

Yet, when crypto comes from another platform, the network can process the transaction without asking the recipient's permission.

FinCEN acknowledges that limitation in the order, and Binance's notice shows what the exchange can do once the funds arrive: it can withhold credit while it reviews the transfer and potentially restrict or close the customer's Binance account.

Any funds left at MEXC stay in that account unless the customer moves them separately.

In a recent development, an on-chain confirmation and exchange-account credit are separate events. Binance indicates deposits from MEXC entities are withheld for review, while outgoing requests are declined.

Blockchain settlement does not force a receiving exchange to credit a customer balance.

Recent findings suggest that binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

Based on the Binance notice published November 10, 2026, and the FinCEN order published November 10 with a December 10 effective date. Inbound path is illustrative; no verified individual customer transfer is claimed.

Recent findings suggest that binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

The business risk for exchanges becomes more serious if customers and professional market makers, the firms that keep buy and sell orders available, lose more ways to fund their accounts or move out the proceeds.

Moving balances between exchanges is part of how those firms keep money available where they need it.

MEXC notes changes at third-party issuers ended its Asia-Pacific card program on Nov. 11 and its Global Card on Nov. 18.

Global Card customers can no longer use their cards for purchases. MEXC says it will credit balances left on the cards to customers' spot accounts within three business days of a Nov. 21 snapshot.

That would leave customers with an exchange balance rather than a working payment card, because spending it with a card requires an issuer.

In France, MEXC had announced its wind-down in October, before the Treasury acted. Its schedule for French accounts stopped euro deposits and withdrawals on Nov. 18, while crypto withdrawals remain available until March 5, 2027.

According to recent reports, trading restrictions begin in batches, and French accounts enter withdrawal-only mode on Jan. 25.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 20, DefiLlama displayed more than $1 billion in MEXC spot trading over 24 hours. That figure measures trading across the platform, including customers outside France, and says little about whether an individual French account can accept deposits, place newly introduced orders, or withdraw its remaining funds.

After Dec. 10, the practical reach of FinCEN's order will depend partly on which banks and exchanges handle a trader's money and which restrictions those firms apply.

Binance has already told customers how it intends to handle MEXC transfers. Other firms may take different approaches, which traders will discover when they try to withdraw a balance, deposit it somewhere else, or spend it through a payment service.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the upcoming i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.

BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

The Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

BMW drove the latest i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.

The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse.

BMW stated the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.

The newly introduced i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.

BMW said the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

The vehicle was driven at all times by a single driver and was not modified in any way, in terms of hardware or software, from the standard i3 available for purchase.

BMW’s new i3 uses a 108.7 kWh battery and Gen6 eDrive system that provides a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

With a drag coefficient of just 0.21, the upcoming i3 is the most aerodynamically efficient BMW vehicle to date.

In the US, BMW said the fresh 2027 i3 50 xDrive will offer an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 468 miles.

With an 800V architecture, the electric sedan can add nearly 262 miles (423 km) of range (WLTP) in about 10 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds up to 400 kW. In the US, the i3 has a built-in NACS port.

Very reasonable. I've been with NK iX3 from Spain to Estonia and the experience is real - low consumption, great comfort and really fast charging. And there are more and more high speed chargers every month.

Sources indicate that like the new iX3, the i3 features BMW’s Neue Klasse interior design. The setup consists of BMW’s massive 43″ Panoramic Vision display that spans the base of the windshield and a 17.9″ floating central infotainment display.

The upcoming BMW i3 50 xDrive is on sale in Germany starting at €65,900 with a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

In the US, the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive and 2027 iX3 50 xDrive are available to order, both starting at $61,500.

Tech Report: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam delay reveals a troubling pattern behind its biggest network upgrades

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.
  • 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.
  • In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached new highs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.

On Nov. 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.

In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached new highs.

“Nobody did a bad job, but I think we fooled ourselves, twice.”.

His findings show that Glamsterdam was assigned the shortest development timeline in years despite being Ethereum's most ambitious upgrade by several measures.

According to Wahrstätter, monthly contributions to Ethereum's technical specifications have increased between twofold and 3.5-fold since 2024, reflecting a substantial acceleration in development activity.

Recent findings suggest that the improvement has extended to testing. Glamsterdam completed 12 development networks, or devnets, in 160 days, compared with seven devnets over 285 days for Pectra, an earlier Ethereum upgrade.

However, Wahrstätter argued that the acceleration has created another problem: developers can now produce specifications, code and tests faster than their colleagues can review them and understand their implications.

That challenge has become more pronounced with Glamsterdam's unprecedented size. The upgrade contains approximately 6,080 lines of execution-layer specifications, compared with 2,318 for Prague, the previous record.

Sources indicate that in a separate count of proposal specifications, Wahrstätter put two of Glamsterdam's most key changes, enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) and block-level access lists (BALs), at approximately 11,900 and 9,300 lines, respectively. The other 16 proposals collectively represent about 3,600 lines.

The complexity is also reflected in EIP-8037, a proposal that changes how Ethereum charges for creating new blockchain state. Although its specifications contain roughly 1,700 lines, the proposal requires approximately 30,000 lines of tests, more than any other proposal included in the upgrade.

Together, this illustrates why faster code production has failed to produce a corresponding acceleration in network upgrades.

Sources indicate that indeed, Wahrstätter's historical analysis demonstrated that every Ethereum upgrade since Dencun has taken more than 400 days from finalizing its scope to reaching mainnet. For context, the three most recent upgrades took between 433 and 475 days, even though their technical scope was smaller than Glamsterdam's.

Despite that record, Glamsterdam was given a development target of just 320 days, substantially shorter than the timelines achieved by previous upgrades.

Wahrstätter found that virtually every Ethereum upgrade with an declared target had missed its deadline. Fusaka was the exception, but only after developers removed Ethereum Object Format (EOF), a major component originally planned for inclusion.

Pectra similarly required developers to divide its original scope across separate upgrades.

It has been revealed that glamsterdam took a different approach. Developers kept adding proposals to successive testing environments while work on its two main components, ePBS and BALs, continued.

Unlike earlier upgrades, the team made no comparable reduction in scope to protect its development timeline.

Consequently, Glamsterdam reached public testing before its specifications had stabilized, creating additional work at a stage when developers would ordinarily be preparing for deployment.

Wahrstätter's analysis showed that Ethereum upgrades between Altair and Deneb recorded no specification changes after their first public testnet.

Sources indicate that pectra recorded two changes, while Fusaka recorded one. Glamsterdam registered 10 in just six weeks.

According to recent reports, the difference also appeared in client development. Work on Pectra declined substantially after public testing began, whereas Glamsterdam-related activity increased 34% following its Sepolia activation, alongside a 25% rise in client commits.

Those late changes became particularly consequential after security researchers identified problems involving EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which alter how Ethereum charges for certain operations.

Sources indicate that the proposals could disrupt assumptions embedded in existing smart contracts, prompting developers to postpone Glamsterdam's Oct. 26 activation on the Hoodi testnet.

The setback has pushed Glamsterdam's expected interval between its first public testnet and mainnet activation beyond 100 days, compared with the 4- to 10-week window typical of previous upgrades, according to Wahrstätter.

In a recent development, during their Nov. 19 meeting, Ethereum developers tentatively targeted Dec. 16 or 17 for Hoodi testing, with mid-January 2027 emerging as the earliest possible mainnet date if the specification stays unchanged.

Wahrstätter argued that preventing further delays would require developers to base release targets on historical performance and set firm deadlines for dropping unfinished features and completing specifications before public testing begins.

In a recent development, he also questioned treating successful devnet deployments as evidence that proposals were sufficiently mature for inclusion in an upgrade. He mentioned:.

“I'm sure we can ship faster, but for that, we must ship smaller.”.

The next decision comes Nov. 26, when Ethereum's core developers are expected to determine whether Glamsterdam can proceed with its proposed December Hoodi activation.

A further postponement would place additional pressure on a release schedule that has already extended well beyond its original target.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • WHEN YOU THINK about a lover’s touch, your brain might jump to a pair of hands lingering around the hips—which might explain the origin of the term "love handles." It’s a cute nickname, but you’d probably describe love handles themselves as anything but cute.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WHEN YOU THINK about a lover’s touch, your brain might jump to a pair of hands lingering around the hips—which might explain the origin of the term "love handles." It’s a cute nickname, but you’d probably describe love handles themselves as anything but cute.

Sources indicate that the term refers to the pesky fat that sits on top of your hip bones, and lots of guys want it gone. “Many men are concerned about how to lose weight in their midsection. I let them know that their body has an android distribution, or male-like, weight distribution,” claims Fatima Cody Stanford, M.D., M.P.H., obesity medicine physician and Men's Health advisor.

While there’s no way to lose fat from your midsection only without medical intervention, there are several ways to bring down your overall body fat which will pull from all areas. If losing your love handles is what will help boost your confidence and make you a healthier, happier version of yourself, that's a fine goal to have. Just remember that there's more to health than how you look, and you can set your sights on other outcomes, too (like getting stronger more generally or something like body recomposition more specifically).

It has been revealed that LOVE HANDLES ARE what most people commonly call the bundle of subcutaneous fat that lies just above your pant line, sitting directly under the skin. That’s actually good news, because it means it’s not the dangerous kind of fat, called visceral fat, that can sit on your organs and put unnecessary (and life-threatening) pressure on them. Adipose fat, such as the love handles, can act as energy deposits. When our bodies lose other energy intake (food), we can use these deposits to power our bodily functions.

Sources indicate that even though our bodies have good intentions when collecting these love handles, it doesn’t mean they’re impossible to lose. But it will involve a solid calorie deficit and some effort in the gym.

Recent findings suggest that there are a few shortcuts you can take, but they're extreme, and not something that we'd generally recommend. Liposuction is one of these options. More recently, men have turned to non-invasive treatments, the most popular of which feature either freezing or heating the stubborn fatty areas off the body. Some guys might also turn to using drugs like a GLP-1 (which can’t target one specific problem area), if a doctor recommends their use. These treatments are expensive and might be a bridge too far, unless you're really desperate.

Besides, by cutting corners, you'll miss out on the fitness gains you'd make along the way using other methods, which will hopefully become a reason you're training, regardless of the aesthetic payoff. If getting rid of love handles without special treatments is your goal, you'll have to work hard—and you'll have to work smart, too.

One method that is not smart and won't work is spot reduction. The theory is that if you focus all of your attention on one specific area in your training (for instance, doing hundreds of crunches for you midsection), you'll be able to burn off the fat in just that area.

Industry observers note that but that's not how your body works. What you can do is lose fat more generally, then build up muscle where you might not have had it before—but for that to work, you'll have to do that smart, hard work. That’s also the case for GLP-1 use. If you go that route, make sure you understand how to train with a program like the MH GLP-1 Muscle Growth initiative.

HERE’S A BLUEPRINT to ditch your stubborn love handles from former Men's Health fitness advisor Craig Ballantyne, C.S.C.S.

Recent findings suggest that studies have shown that interval-based exercise programs, most specifically high intensity interval training (HIIT), are more effective for burning off your love handles than steady state cardio. Instead of running for miles on end without any clear goal, fine tune your work and rest periods to strip away the fat.

So what type of interval program should you use? You can use a jump rope, or apply the principles to running or weight room work. Ballantyne recommends this setup to banish that pesky midsection fat:.

After a thorough warmup, alternate between 20 seconds of hard exercise and 40 seconds recovery. Repeat that pattern 6 to 8 times. Afterwards, finish with 5 to 10 minutes of cooldown exercise.

If you have extra time, do 10 minutes of regular cardio pace.

Recent findings suggest that even though Ballantyne recommended cardio for a cool down, he's wary of its effectiveness when performed alone. Extended periods of steady state cardio, like jogging, won’t do much to cut down your spare tire. "It's not going to work as well as interval training," Ballantyne mentioned.

It has been revealed that this is related to another issue, according to Ballantyne: Many guys don't have enough muscle in the first place. Losing love handles, like bodybuilding, is a game of illusion. Muscle on your chest and back can essentially "hide" excess fat in your love handle area.

Industry observers note that "So most guys are “skinny-fat,” and then try to lose love handles with cardio only, and basically become even smaller versions of themselves—but still skinny-fat," Ballantyne remarked. "It's better to use intervals and weight training to gain muscle and lose fat at the same time—which IS possible—and change your body's overall appearance.".

"Ab exercises like crunches are generally a waste of time," Ballantyne remarked. The problem is, you’re only working the muscles around your lower spine with crunches and situps.

Instead, you should build up your core with moves that focus on spinal stability, like planks and hollow body holds. Check out this quick video about the way your core muscles function for an idea of what you should be aiming for:.

According to recent reports, want a smarter core workout in general? Check out Epic Abs, the program from MH fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. that inspired this video.

Industry observers note that while you're cutting down your midsection, do yourself a solid and work on some other areas of your body that can take attention away from your ample hips. Build up your pecs, lats, deltoids, and traps to create the illusion of smaller love handles.

"Most guys don't have enough muscle to focus on just losing weight," Ballantyne mentioned, "so every guy must build some muscle in these areas.".

Industry observers note that how can you build the muscle and lose fat at the same time? You're hoping to "culk," so you should start by training hard, eating properly, and sticking to a consistent program.

Ballantyne also recommended a plan based around two to three total body workouts per week. Use five exercises per workout (one lower body, one upper push, one lower body single leg, one upper pulling, one total body ab exercise). Do that as a circuit three times through, with eight to 12 reps per exercise. Finish with interval training.

For best results, follow a plan that fits your unique training needs. Use our Workout Finder below to get a personalized recommendation based on your age, fitness level, and other key factors.

You can't neglect nutrition if you're looking to lose fat. After all, losing fat means burning more calories then you take in, or creating a calorie deficit. Here’s how to calculate a healthy calorie deficit based on your body and goals.

There are easy eating hacks you can incorporate into your daily routine to cut calories while still enjoying yourself and staying satisfied. Eliminating foods you love is an unsustainable way to live. "Negotiate with yourself on what you are willing to do without or do with less of," states Leslie Bonci, R.D., sports dietitian for Kansas City Chiefs.

Prioritize and optimize protein, fiber, healthy fats, and produce to fill up. Protein and fiber help you stay fuller, longer—which may reduce snacking in between meals. When choosing grains, pick the higher fiber choices like quinoa, oatmeal, and whole wheat pastas. Incorporate more beans into your salads, soups, and even blend and add to sauces. Include a fruit or a veggie at every occasion.

When it comes to snacking, focus on foods that will make you chew longer and eat slower, like jerky or apples. Bean dips with veggies are also a quick and easy snack that will load up the fiber and protein with little calories.

To really find a custom nutrition initiative that will work best with your body, talk to a registered dietitian.

We don’t need to tell you that losing weight is no walk in the park. Accomplishing your goals will take a balance of overhauled nutrition, exercise, and recovery practices to complete the equation and finally shed some of those pounds. You might find it tough to do any of those things on your own.

Working with a professional can help provide some much needed accountability and guidance. Doctors who specialize in weight loss, nutritionists, dietitians, and personal trainers can all help you get to where you want to be. They can tailor your workouts and meal aims to better match your genetic makeup and goals. Don’t be afraid to ask for help if the task feels daunting.

SORRY TO BREAK it to you—doing loads of side bends and Russian twists won’t melt away your love handles. It’s impossible to lose fat on one portion of your body by exercising the muscles in that area. The concept is called spot training, or spot reduction—and it doesn’t work.

What does work is incorporating high-velocity compound movements into your workouts. Compound movements are exercises that require multiple muscle groups working together. These kinds of moves will burn a lot of calories, aiding in creating the calorie deficit you need to burn fat all over. Here are 6 of our favorites.

This move lights up your body head to toe, and ramps up your heart rate in the process. Not only will med ball slams aid in the fat loss process, but they’ll help you take a little aggression out on your worst days.

Sets and Reps: Aim for 2 to 3 sets of 30 second sets, either as a warm up or programmed into your next conditioning circuit.

The dumbbell snatch is one of the best movements for building full body power and strength. Almost your entire body has to work to power the weight up and overhead.

Sets and Reps: Aim for 3 sets of 3 to 5 reps with a heavy weight, or build it into a conditioning set by doing 30 seconds of work, 30 seconds of rest with a medium weight.

Industry observers note that the kettlebell swing is a fundamental core exercise that works practically every muscle in your body. Be careful about ramping up the weight too quickly though—this move has a ton of subtleties that are vital to the safety of the movement.

Sets and Reps: Do 4 sets of 10 to 12 reps with a heavy weight, or build it into a conditioning set by doing 30 seconds of work, 30 seconds of rest with a medium weight.

Burpees are infamous for a reason. It looks simple, but do it the right way and you’ll feel way more of a challenge than you’d expect.

Sets and Reps: Aim 3 to 4 rounds of 20 seconds on, 40 seconds off, or build it into a conditioning circuit.

Mountain climbers are a staple core exercise that will challenge your upper body too as you maintain that high plank position.

Sets and Reps: Set a timer for 6 minutes and aim for 20 seconds of work, 10 seconds of rest for a good core burn, build it into a conditioning circuit.

This multi-joint movement combines a front squat and a push press to incorporate the whole body to build power and strength—and torch calories, too.

Sets and Reps: Aim for 3 sets of 6 to 8 reps, build it into a conditioning circuit for 30 seconds of work, 30 seconds of rest.

Breaking: Meet SHRINCS: Bitcoin's Emerging Frontrunner for a Post-Quantum Signature

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.
  • It has been revealed that “We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, mentioned in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP).
  • Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.

It has been revealed that “We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, mentioned in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP). “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.".

Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

According to recent reports, that said, the scheme comes with trade-offs, most notably by introducing potential security vulnerabilities at the implementation level if misused. The scheme combines two spending paths: a small, more efficient stateful signature option and a larger, more costly stateless path with fewer security risks on the implementation side.

Although stateful signatures are compact, preserving Bitcoin’s ability to process transactions efficiently, a user can trigger a critical failure—where an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal funds if a one-time state is accidentally reused. Because SHRINCS’ stateful path relies on one-time keys that can only safely sign a single transaction, wallet developers must carefully track each key’s state.

Recent findings suggest that “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” Nick told Head of MARA Foundation Isabel Foxen Duke during a recent appearance on MARA Foundation TV. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”.

According to Nick, for SHRINCS to work safely in the real world, its specification and corresponding wallet implementations must automatically enforce the stateless path fallback in any situation where a state counter could possibly be compromised.

While some people might gravitate toward stateless signatures out of caution, Nick warns that widespread adoption could bloat the blockchain and drive up fees across the network.

Bitcoin’s current ECDSA signatures are typically 71 bytes long (and Taproot Schnorr signatures are 64 bytes). Under SHRINCS, stateful signatures are anywhere from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while stateless ones are 5,777 bytes. That mentioned, optimizations of both signature paths have been accelerating with the support of AI-based research, Nick noted.

Industry observers note that “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very massive signatures,” he noted. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”.

As the SHRINCS working group—which includes researchers backed by nonprofits including Brink and OpenSats—continues to refine the proposal’s specification, Blockstream researchers stress that getting the cryptographic foundation right is only half the battle.

In a recent development, whether the broader Bitcoin ecosystem is ready to embrace SHRINCS’ inherent trade-offs will depend heavily on feedback from the network’s stakeholders in the months ahead. Meanwhile, Nick and Kudinov are requesting review of the proposal and the security analysis.

Industry observers note that andré Beganski is a Senior Content Manager at MARA Foundation, producing content on topics including the intersection of quantum computing and cryptography. He has previously worked for Decrypt.

#41496. Breaking: Menopause Was a Hushed Conversation—Until Gen X Changed Everything

Breaking: Menopause Was a Hushed Conversation—Until Gen X Changed Everything

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, sharon Cancio, 28, didn’t grow up knowing much about menopause.
  • Cancio didn’t start connecting the dots until she came off birth control at 25 and noticed how dramatically her own mood changed around her cycle.
  • Recent findings suggest that these discussions are a far cry from what conversations around menopause used to look like: nonexistent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sharon Cancio, 28, didn’t grow up knowing much about menopause. She didn’t learn anything about it in school, nor from the women in her family. But when she was a teenager, she started noticing her mother’s mood shifting. Around her mid-to-late 40s, “she became much snappier, more easily irritated, and sometimes just seemed angry in a way that felt completely different from the mom I remembered growing up,” she recalls. “I genuinely thought life had simply worn her down.”.

Cancio didn’t start connecting the dots until she came off birth control at 25 and noticed how dramatically her own mood changed around her cycle. Once she realized her mother had entered perimenopause, she went down an internet rabbit hole to learn about it. Women were discussing—in detail—what was happening to their bodies on TikTok and Reddit. Some women were going through menopause early, others were seeking answers for their symptoms.

Recent findings suggest that these discussions are a far cry from what conversations around menopause used to look like: nonexistent. In the past, there wasn’t much education—or even real discussion—on what happens to the female body after 40, forcing women to hustle through hot flashes and mood swings behind closed doors.

But within the last few years, there’s been a shift: Gen X women are the first to go through this hormonal transition in the age of social media—and they’re not afraid to talk about their experiences, says Gillan Goddard, MD, an endocrinologist and an adjunct assistant professor of medicine at the NYU Langone Hospital. They’re educating an entire generation of younger women in the process. Posts about brain fog, inconsistent sleep patterns, and unfamiliar-feeling bodies have become the first real health literacy that this generation’s daughters, Gen Zers, have gotten about their own hormonal futures. These small conversations have major implications when it comes to learning more about their future health.

Recent findings suggest that the lack of menopause education starts in classrooms: Almost all U.S. states require teenagers to learn about puberty, reproductive health, and sexual disease prevention through sex education classes. But the content and depth of those classes may not favor women’s health: A 2024 study in the Journal of School Health looked at the state of menstrual health education in U.S. K-12 public schools. Researchers analyzed the education standards from each state’s Department of Education site, searching terms like “menstruation,” “menopause,” “period,” “reproduction,” and “puberty.” It found that menstrual health education—especially menopause—is profoundly rare.

Sources indicate that there’s also a lack of menopause education in medical schools. Only 31.3 percent of U.S. ob-gyn residency programs include a menopause curriculum, according to a 2023 study in Menopause. The result resembles a serious disconnect: The transition affects nearly half of the population, but the majority of the doctors tasked with treating menopause have received almost no training on how to do it.

Menopause just isn’t prioritized during residency training. Instead, the “focus during training was placed on surgical skills and labor and delivery responsibilities, both considered more urgent and time-consuming,” says Alyssa Dweck, MD, chief medical officer of Bonafide Health and a Menopause Society Certified Practitioner located in Latest York City. Ob-gyns can earn certifications in (peri)menopause, from organizations including the Menopause Society and Integrative Women’s Health Institute—but they’re not required. Clinicians should have more comprehensive training in medical school and beyond, says Dr. Dweck. But there should also be more funding and resources for women’s health research for treatment options.

Industry observers note that when doctors aren’t familiar with menopause, “mood changes, cognitive changes, and body aches are often misunderstood or ignored,” says Dr. Goddard. This can lead to misdiagnoses, and to women not receiving proper treatment for symptoms caused by menopause. This is pretty common: A 2025 survey conducted by health care firm Biote of over 1,000 women ages 30 to 60 in the U.S. found that 39 percent of women have been misdiagnosed and prescribed medication by a provider for conditions like depression.

TikTok and Instagram have filled the menopause education void in the U.S. Conversations about life in menopause have spread awareness about what the condition is actually like, crushing stigmas. This visibility is not only helping younger viewers learn what they can expect later in life—it’s also helping mothers start more health-forward conversations with their daughters.

Recent findings suggest that milan Parker, 25, has always had open conversations about health with her mom. “She’s always been really honest with me about what she’s going through, even the more personal parts that people sometimes consider taboo,” she says. But social media increased this dynamic tenfold: Parker’s mother underwent a hysterectomy due to fibroids at 48, which made her enter early menopause. Following the surgery, her mother joined a menopause support group on Facebook. “Seeing that there were women all across the country going through similar things made her more open to talking to me about it,” Parker says.

For instance, Parker’s mom finally explained how debilitating her hot flashes really were. (She’d stopped going on trips with her because she was embarrassed about looking sweaty.) “There were times when I thought maybe my mom just didn’t want to go out with me,” she says. “I’m really grateful that she made it something we could actually talk about instead of something that had to stay a secret.”.

According to recent reports, for daughters, it can be hard to watch their mothers struggle in menopause and not know how to help, but the experience can also help them grow closer. “The emotional experience can be a mix of empathy, grief, anxiety, and closeness,” says Ashley Peña, LCSW, a clinical social worker and the vice president of outpatient operations at Mission Connection.

Even though Cancio’s mom didn’t tell her when she was going through menopause, the experience helped her gain compassion for her mother and better understand her own body. “As a teenager, I honestly thought she was just becoming grumpy or ‘getting old,’ which I feel terrible admitting now,” she indicates. “As an adult woman, I have so much more empathy.”.

It has been revealed that having a raw look at what menopause is actually like—whether through a screen or a conversation with their mother—shapes how younger women view aging and how to prepare themselves for what’s ahead. Hearing that they may one day inevitably experience sleepless nights, sudden anger, brain fog, and the loss of identity can be scary, to say the least. But “open conversation about menopause helps women hear the full scope of menopause experiences and how women dealt effectively with their symptoms,” Dr. Goddard says. It can make the condition sound less scary to younger women.

Sources indicate that in fact, growing conversations around menopause can actually inspire younger women to learn about it earlier. “I am seeing patients of all ages, Gen Z included, who have become more inquisitive and engaged in their health overall,” Dr. Dweck indicates. Some of her young patients have told her they’ve already started talking to their older relatives about menopause and hormone health. They’re also more open about discussing fertility and egg freezing.

Even though menopause is now common dinner table conversation, the root of the (non-communication) glitch still needs to be fixed. “The only way we normalize talking about women’s health is by talking about it,” Cancio indicates. “Ask questions, stay curious, and don’t be afraid to learn from women who have already been through it.”.

It has been revealed that mothers going through (peri)menopause can have a series of casual conversations about it with their kids. (The earlier, the better.) They can keep the conversation casual and tailored to the child’s developmental age. For instance, moms with children under the age of 13 can briefly mention that they’re “going through a body change.” Then, as the kids get older, they can talk more openly about what they’re experiencing, states Dr. Dweck. Encouraging their children to ask questions about menopause can also build empathy and normalize conversations surrounding health.

Industry observers note that on the flip side, Parker wants Gen Z women to pay attention to what their mothers are going through, and not wait until the right moment to spark a conversation. “Having those conversations with my mom has made that feel a lot less scary and a lot more human,” she states. “Every stage of life comes sooner than you think, so it’s worth paying attention to your health long before you feel like you have to.”.

Sources indicate that cancio didn’t feel like she could have those conversations with her mom, which is part of what inspired her to start making content around women’s health topics for younger women. “I started thinking about the girl who was sitting at home Googling something because she was too embarrassed to ask her mom, or the girl who thought something was wrong with her because nobody had ever explained that what she was experiencing was normal,” she states.

In a recent development, even though the way that Gen Z is learning about menopause isn’t perfect—whether through a viral post or their mother—it’s still a step in the right direction. By doing her part, Cancio hopes to have a completely different relationship with her future daughter “where no topic about her body is off limits and she never feels like she has to search for answers alone.”.

#41494. Latest Update: BYD and Geely approached FIA about a 12th F1 team, states Ben Sulayem

Latest Update: BYD and Geely approached FIA about a 12th F1 team, states Ben Sulayem

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed.
  • It has been revealed that but there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither company has a deal.
  • “One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem mentioned of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem named the two Chinese automakers while speaking at the New Economy Forum in Madrid, as first reported by Grande Prêmio.

It has been revealed that but there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither company has a deal. The FIA is also pushing F1 toward the kind of engine an EV maker has the least reason to build.

“One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem mentioned of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.

Industry observers note that he said he suggested that BYD buy an existing team instead of starting a latest one. BYD wasn’t interested in that route. It wants its own team, so Ben Sulayem told the firm to come back with a “serious proposal” that highlights the project can work.

It has been revealed that he also made it clear that Chinese manufacturers won’t get special treatment. Any bid would go through the same process as other prospective entrants, and the rules won’t be rewritten to suit them. Right now, there’s no expansion process at all: the FIA isn’t actively looking for a 12th team.

Still, Ben Sulayem repeated that he’d like F1’s next newcomer to come from China, pointing to the country’s EV technology and the Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai.

This isn’t latest for BYD. Back in March, we reported that BYD was exploring a Formula 1 entry, either by buying a team or building one from scratch.

Sources indicate that in April, executive vice president Stella Li remarked BYD had met F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali in Shanghai and that an entry was “something we’re discussing.” By July, the tone had cooled. Li said “the dream is always there, but we don’t have a concrete agenda,” and special advisor Alfredo Altavilla set a clear condition: “We will never participate in Formula 1 just to put a sticker on the side of a car.”.

Altavilla stated BYD would only consider F1 to the extent its technology can serve the sport.

Industry observers note that geely is the new name here. The group sold 3.02 million vehicles last year and owns Volvo, Polestar, and Lotus, a brand with decades of F1 history. It’s also heading into Canada next year as Chinese automakers push hard into new markets.

In a recent development, the last newcomer, Cadillac, took a long road. The FIA opened an expression-of-interest process in 2023, and GM’s team only joined the grid as the 11th team this season, running Ferrari power until its own power unit arrives. Audi got in the other way, by taking over Sauber.

Here’s where it gets awkward for an EV maker. The 2026 F1 power units split output roughly 50/50 between the combustion engine and electric power, with the MGU-K jumping to 350 kW.

The FIA is already walking that back. In June, it agreed to shift the split to 60-40 in favor of combustion for 2027 and 2028. And Ben Sulayem has been pushing for V8 engines running on sustainable fuel with “minor electrification” for the next rules cycle, starting in 2031 at the latest, possibly 2030. Domenicali indicates F1 should have a package ready to discuss by the end of this year.

So the FIA president wants a Chinese EV maker on the grid, while pushing a rulebook that makes their main strength less relevant.

We like the idea of BYD or Geely in F1. Chinese automakers have the money and the engineers, and they badly need brand prestige outside China. BYD in particular has been on a performance push with Yangwang, and F1 would be the loudest possible way to tell Europe it’s not just a cheap car brand.

they look for visibility/recognition on the world stage, regardless EVs. And in some (primitive) markets they market themselves as hybrids automakers, not as EV automakers.

They will make a hybrid power unit (which they already make anyway) to comply with the backward F1 regulations.

But Ben Sulayem’s comments don’t move things much. There’s no entry process, BYD has already turned down his main suggestion, and Geely’s interest is a name dropped at a conference, not a bid.

In a recent development, A Chinese would likely be good for F1 as well. Motorsports are on the rise in China, and that would be the cherry on top in helping popularize the sport in the world’s largest market.

The bigger problem is the engine. Altavilla was clear that BYD isn’t interested in slapping a logo on a car. It wants F1 to showcase its technology, and BYD’s technology is batteries and electric drive. The FIA’s V8 push goes the other way. It’s hard to sell an EV giant on a sport that’s reducing the electric part of the powertrain.

If you’re following how fast EV tech is moving, from BYD’s batteries to F1’s hybrid power units, you can put some of that tech to work at home: pairing an EV with rooftop solar can cut your driving costs to nearly zero.
